## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Which measurement is the gate — total LLM wall clock (sum of per-call elapsed, this item's AC1 wording) or end-to-end wall clock (the baseline doc's regression-gate definition, which also includes scan/execute/`wl sync` time)?
  **Answer (deferred — OPEN QUESTION, non-blocking):** preserved the item's AC1 wording (**total LLM wall clock**, consistent with the parent AC6 gate which is measured the same way) and recorded the end-to-end figure alongside in the baseline doc. **Recommended:** keep LLM wall clock as the gate and report end-to-end as secondary context — the committed gate's "end to end ≤ 10 min" was the original headline but the corpus-based gate the parent epic actually enforced is LLM wall clock. Producer to confirm at plan review. Source: `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` § Regression gate + this item's AC1; research: both measurements are already recorded in the 2026-10-23 table.
- **Q:** If a clean-room run on the healthy proxy's `plan`/`code` models still cannot reach ≤ 10 min, is a remote fast model (e.g. `deepseek-v4-flash`, already in `.pi-config/agent/models.json` and seen in historical audit logs) permitted, or must the lever stay local-proxy-bound?
  **Answer (deferred — OPEN QUESTION, non-blocking):** assumed **local-proxy-only** for this item (ACs' "healthy-proxy" framing); the parent epic left remote routing as an open question and this item does not reopen it. **Recommended:** local fast alias only; keep remote out of scope to avoid breadth creep — flip only with producer authorisation at plan review.   **Answer (deferred — OPEN QUESTION, non-blocking):** assumed the **small-item shape** per the committed regression gate's definition ("small item, 1–5 ACs"). **Recommended:** keep the committed gate's definition; a heavy single-item audit is not in scope for this item. ## Plan (decomposition) — 2026-10-27

The item is decomposed into three dependency-ordered children, one **verification-first** slice followed by two **conditional** lever slices. Vertical-slice check: child 1 = verification + docs + tests; children 2 and 3 each cut through code + tests + docs + measurement evidence. No phase is a single horizontal layer. Between phases a session must review the next child's description against the new measurement before starting it (the child ACs cite the "baseline: the Lane A/Lane B figures", which must be the figures actually recorded).

### Reuse rather than new machinery

## Problem

The audit merge gate (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` → `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`) mines every hex token from the work item's description and comments and keeps those that resolve to **any** git object in the owning repo (`_commit_object_exists`). It does not filter by which ref the commit is reachable from.

When an item's text cites commits that exist only on `refs/worklog/data`, its backup refs, or other non-`dev` refs (e.g. a worklog history-rewrite item quoting incident-era SHAs), `_verify_merged_in_dev` finds no ancestor of `origin/dev` among the candidates and the gate proceeds to `_integrate_into_dev`, which cherry-picks those commits onto a worktree at `origin/dev` — conflicting and failing the audit closed with a spurious `Ready to close: No` merge-gate blocker.

## Observed (2026-10-23, SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC)

- Audit run 1: `git cherry-pick 345ea154a -> rc=1` conflict; verdict `Ready to close: No` (merge-gate blocker). `345ea154a` is a `refs/worklog/data` commit, never a `dev` commit.
- Workaround applied: the item description now records a real `dev` commit (`92fee5c30`, an ancestor of `origin/dev`), so the ancestor scan short-circuits to merged before any cherry-pick. Fragile — it depends on authors remembering to cite a `dev` commit and on the scan order.
- Related (already completed): SA-0MTQAF62U0085BEV (foreign hex that is not an object at all) and SA-0MTECRNGR000VKLV (decimal literals mined as SHAs). This is a third variant: the token **is** a commit object, but not on the delivery ref.

## Desired behaviour

- Restrict integration-evidence candidates to commits reachable from the item's delivery surface (branches matching `wl-<id>-*`, and any commit that is an ancestor of `origin/dev` or of a referenced feature branch) — or, at minimum, skip candidates not reachable from any `refs/heads/*` / `origin/*` ref of the owning repo, recording the skip as evidence.
- Commits reachable only from `refs/worklog/*`, `refs/backup/*` or unreachable objects must never be cherry-picked onto `dev`.
- Keep fail-open behaviour for evidence-less items and fail-closed behaviour for genuinely unmerged feature work.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1:** A work item whose description cites commits reachable only from `refs/worklog/data` (or a backup ref) does NOT trigger `_integrate_into_dev`; the gate records a skip note naming each excluded candidate and its non-delivery ref.
2. **AC2:** Regression test (in `skill/audit/tests/`) builds a fixture repo with a `dev` branch, a `refs/worklog/data` commit and a description citing that commit, and asserts `_phase_merge_gate` passes without invoking cherry-pick (no stray worktree, no blocker).
3. **AC3:** Existing behaviour is unchanged for: the real delivered commit (ancestor of `origin/dev` → merged), genuinely unmerged feature-branch work (still integrates), and evidence-less items (fail-open).
data.title: Audit merge gate treats commits on other refs (worklog/backup) as dev integration evidence

## Problem
acquireFileLock() (~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts) removes a lock whose acquiredAt is older than DEFAULT_MAX_LOCK_AGE_MS (5 min) even when the holder PID is alive on the same host. A long wl sync (fetch/merge/push over a slow network or a large store) therefore has its lock stolen mid-operation, and two writers proceed concurrently: the sync then writes back its pre-operation snapshot over whatever the stealer committed (the general lost-update class that WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1 closed for short operations).

## Why it was not fixed in SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ
The claim-hold guard now prevents the user-visible damage (a reverted claim), but non-claim field writes are still exposed in that window.

## Suggested direction
Treat a same-host live holder as authoritative (no age-expiry), keep age-expiry for dead-PID / foreign-host / unparseable locks, and/or refresh the lock (acquiredAt heartbeat) during long syncs. Add a deterministic regression test using the sync-vs-mutation.test.ts git-shim parking technique plus a back-dated lock file.

## Key Files
- ~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts
- ~/projects/ContextHub/src/commands/sync.ts
- ~/projects/ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts

## Goal

As an operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`, I want the CPU / memory / I/O stall pressure metrics to report real values, so the diagnosis is based on the kernel's own pressure-stall signal instead of silently losing three of its twelve metrics.

## Problem statement

`skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/metrics.py::_read_proc_pressure()` never matches a PSI line, so `cpu_pressure`, `memory_pressure` and `io_pressure` are permanently rendered `n/a` ("unavailable (non-Linux or kernel missing pressure stall info)") even when `/proc/pressure/*` is present and readable — three of the twelve before-table metrics are dead weight and the pressure analysis in Step 2 can never fire on stall data.

## Users

- **Operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`** — "As an operator, I want the before table to show the kernel's stall percentages so I can tell CPU contention from memory or I/O starvation without guessing."
- **Agent triaging a slow host** — "As an agent, I want the numeric pressure value in the metrics dict so `pressure_analysis.analyze_pressures()` can surface a real pressure with contributors instead of skipping the metric."
- **Skill maintainer** — "As a maintainer, I want PSI parsing covered by verbatim-content unit tests so a wrong fixture can't mask the bug again."

## Evidence (verified)

Re-verified on this host (16-core Ubuntu, 2026-10-23): all three collectors return `None` while PSI is readable.

```
some avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=84206005618   # /proc/pressure/cpu
some avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=64384303      # /proc/pressure/memory (some)
full avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=35437059      # /proc/pressure/memory (full)
some avg10=0.05 avg60=0.11 avg300=0.10 total=398915844     # /proc/pressure/io (some)
full avg10=0.05 avg60=0.11 avg300=0.10 total=270870893     # /proc/pressure/io (full)
```

Original discovery run (2026-10-21) showed genuine CPU `some` pressure of `avg10=11.58` alongside load 11.92 on 16 cores — real signal was thrown away.

## Root cause

```python
for line in lines:
    if line.startswith("avg"):        # never true — lines start with "some " / "full "
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) >= 4:
            return float(parts[1])    # tokens are avg10=<v> etc., not bare numbers
return None
```

Two independent defects: the prefix test can never match, and the value token needs `split("=")` (not whitespace index 1). The existing unit test passes only because it feeds a fabricated two-line fixture (`some:stuff` followed by `avg10  60.00 60.00 60.00`) that matches the buggy parser rather than real kernel output.

## Desired change

1. `_read_proc_pressure(key: str, which: str = "some") -> float | None` parses real PSI output, returning the `avg10` stall percentage of the requested `some`/`full` line; returns `None` when the file is missing/empty/unparsable or the requested line is absent.
2. `pressure_specs` gains a per-metric line selector (decided: **`cpu` → `some`; `memory` → `full`; `io` → `full`**) so the semantic choice is explicit in code.
3. Each metric's `description` names the line used and its basis, e.g. `"CPU stall pressure (some avg10, % of time any task stalled)"`, so the table is self-documenting; the `n/a` description states which line was requested.
4. `memory_pressure` gets its **own** `config.yaml` block (and `config.py::_DEFAULTS` entry) calibrated for `full`-line semantics — `warning: 5`, `critical: 20` — replacing the current accidental mapping to `memory_usage` 80/95.
5. `SKILL.md` metric table gains a line-selection column and documents the `some` vs `full` semantics, the new `memory_pressure` block, and the no-fallback degradation rule.

## Implementation plan (test-first, single vertical slice)

**Decomposition decision: no child work items.** The change is one Small, self-contained vertical slice (parser → wiring → config → docs → tests) confined to a single skill; splitting it would add coordination overhead without reducing risk. Test-first ordering is expressed as the sequence below and enforced by the build → test → commit gate during implementation.

1. **Failing parser tests first** (`tests/test_metrics.py::TestReadProcPressure`) — delete the fabricated `avg10  60.00 …` fixture, add verbatim kernel samples (cpu `some`-only; memory/io `some` + `full`), asserting the expected `avg10` values and that `which="some"` vs `which="full"` select different lines of the same sample — **AC1**. Verify: new tests fail (RED) against today's `_read_proc_pressure`.
2. **Failure-mode tests** — missing file, present-but-unparsable (`avg10=abc`), requested `full` line absent (documented no-fallback), empty file → `None` — **AC2**.
3. **Parser implementation** (`scripts/metrics.py::_read_proc_pressure(key, which="some")`) — select the `some ` / `full ` line, parse `avg10=<v>` with `split("=")`, return `float`, `None` on any failure — **AC1, AC2**. Verify: steps 1–2 tests GREEN.
4. **Config block** (`scripts/config.py::_DEFAULTS` + `config.yaml`) — add `memory_pressure` (`low: 0`, `warning: 5`, `critical: 20`) calibrated for `full`-line semantics; fix the misleading "Memory Pressure" heading above `memory_usage`; `tests/test_config.py` gains defaults + file-override assertions — **AC5**.
5. **Wiring + description tests** (`collect_metrics`) — `pressure_specs` gains a per-metric line selector (`cpu`→`some`, `memory`→`full`, `io`→`full`) and `memory_pressure` resolves to the new config key; descriptions carry line + basis (e.g. `"CPU stall pressure (some avg10, % of time any task stalled)"`) and the `n/a` description names the requested line; a mocked-PSI test asserts rendered values, statuses and descriptions — **AC3, AC6**.
6. **Documentation** (`SKILL.md`) — line-selection column in the metric table, `some` vs `full` semantics, the new `memory_pressure` block, threshold provenance, the no-fallback degradation rule, and why stall % is not comparable to `memory_usage` % — **AC4, AC5, AC8**.
7. **Real-host verification** — run `scripts/evaluate.py` from the worktree on this PSI-enabled host; numeric `cpu_pressure` / `memory_pressure` / `io_pressure` (no `n/a`); paste the run output into a comment on this item — **AC7**.
8. **Gate** — changed-scope tests via `/skill:test`, and the full suite must pass before any `dev` push — **AC9**.

No phasing boundary is needed: the slice lands as one branch/worktree with a test-first commit series.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25 — `/skill:plan` session `herdr-1792903348-145198-13191`: duplicate-work check found no overlapping item (`SA-0MVLJAG3P0053RJ2` is the deliberate threshold-recalibration follow-up — no AC overlap); AC1–AC9 traced to the five "Desired change" requirements; **AC6 extended** to cover requirement 3's clause that the `n/a` description names the requested line; **AC8 made verifiable** against this repository's actual documentation surfaces (no README or docs-site entry exists for this skill); test-first implementation sequence recorded above; decomposition decision: no child work items (single Small vertical slice).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — `_read_proc_pressure` parses verbatim `/proc/pressure` content and returns the `avg10` percentage for the requested `some`/`full` line; a unit test feeds real cpu (some only) and memory/io (some + full) samples and asserts the expected values, plus that `which="some"` and `which="full"` select different values from the same two-line sample.
- **AC2** — Unit tests cover failure modes: missing file → `None`; present but unparsable (`avg10=abc`) → `None`; requested `full` line absent → `None` (documented no-fallback behaviour); empty file → `None`.
- **AC3** — `collect_metrics()` wires `cpu`→`some`, `memory`→`full`, `io`→`full` and classifies `memory_pressure` against the new `memory_pressure` config block; a unit test with mocked PSI content asserts the rendered numeric values, their statuses, and that the descriptions name the selected line.
- **AC4** — The `some` vs `full` choice per metric is documented in `SKILL.md` and reflected in each metric's `description`; the previously wrong `test_metrics.py` fixture is replaced with verbatim kernel content.
- **AC5** — `memory_pressure` has its own `config.yaml` block and `config.py::_DEFAULTS` entry (with `test_config.py` coverage asserting the defaults and a file override), and `SKILL.md` explains why stall percentage is not comparable to `memory_usage` percentage.
- **AC6** — Degradation is unchanged: non-Linux or PSI-less kernels still yield `None` and an "unavailable" description that names the requested line (requirement 3) with no crash, covered by a test.
- **AC7** — On this PSI-enabled host, a real `scripts/evaluate.py` run renders numeric `cpu_pressure` / `memory_pressure` / `io_pressure` values (no `n/a`); the run output is pasted into a comment on this item.
- **AC8** — All related documentation in this repository is updated: `SKILL.md` (metric table, `some`/`full` semantics, `memory_pressure` block, degradation rule) plus code comments/docstrings in `metrics.py` and `config.py`. This skill has no README and no docs-site/wiki entry today, so no other documentation surface needs an update.
- **AC9** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Repo/ownership:** the skill is canonical here (`skill/machine-hygiene/`), installed to `~/.pi/agent/skills` by `scripts/install_pi.sh`. Do not patch the installed copy by hand; no new copy in another repo. Note the current global install is a real directory rather than the script's symlink — refreshing it (`scripts/install_pi.sh` or equivalent) is part of verifying AC7, not part of the change.
- **Scope:** parser + line-selection semantics + `memory_pressure` thresholds + tests + docs only.
- **Python style:** existing `unittest` + `importlib`-by-path module loading; no new dependencies.
- **No behaviour change** to action execution, approval gating, or table rendering; `tables.py` already renders numeric/n-a correctly.
- **Stable metric keys:** `cpu_pressure` / `memory_pressure` / `io_pressure` names must not change (consumed by `pressure_analysis._PRESSURE_METRICS` and the before/after table).

### Out of scope

- Recalibrating `cpu_pressure` (70/85) and `io_pressure` (50/80) thresholds — split out to SA-0MVLJAG3P0053RJ2.
- Process/thread/swap threshold miscalibration (ContextHub WL-0MVI8YM07002Z9VY) and duplicate proposed-actions (WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ).
- Any change to action execution, approval gating, table layout, or cgroup/systemd resource limiting.

## Existing state

- `scripts/metrics.py` — `_read_proc_pressure(key)` (buggy), `pressure_specs` maps `memory_pressure` → `memory_usage` thresholds.
- `scripts/config.py` — `_DEFAULTS` has `cpu_pressure`, `memory_usage`, `io_pressure`; **no** `memory_pressure`.
- `config.yaml` — documents `memory_usage` under a "Memory Pressure (from /proc/pressure/memory)" heading (misleading), no `memory_pressure` block.
- `SKILL.md` — metric table lists the three pressure metrics with "Percentage thresholds"; no `some`/`full` mention.
- `tests/test_metrics.py` — `TestReadProcPressure` uses the fake `avg10 60.00 …` fixture that locks in the bug.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** Ubuntu/Worklog hosts run kernel ≥ 4.20, where memory and I/O expose both `some` and `full`. Older PSI backports exposing only `some` will render memory/io `n/a` — accepted and documented (no silent fallback to `some`, which would mix severities).
- **Assumption:** `full`-line `avg10` is the actionable signal for memory/io; `warning: 5` / `critical: 20` are starting thresholds to be tuned from real runs (no data exists today because the parser never worked).
- **Risk — silent green:** if thresholds were left at 80/95, `memory_pressure` would parse but never fire; AC5's own block with PSI-calibrated values avoids re-introducing the loss of signal.
- **Risk — noisy amber:** with `full` semantics + low thresholds, a heavily loaded multi-agent host may show persistent amber memory/io pressure; acceptable (it *is* the honest stall signal) but worth watching during AC7 verification.
- **Risk — masked-by-fixture regression:** the current fixture asserts the buggy format; AC4 must delete it rather than adapt it, or the test suite keeps blessing the wrong shape.
- **Scope-creep risk:** switching `io_pressure` to `full` also makes its existing 50/80 thresholds miscalibrated, and `cpu_pressure`'s 70/85 deserve a sanity pass under `some` semantics. Recorded as the linked follow-up **SA-0MVLJAG3P0053RJ2** rather than widening this item.

## Key Files

- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/metrics.py` — `_read_proc_pressure()` (~line 105) gains the `which` selector and real parsing; `pressure_specs` (~line 352) gains the per-metric line choice; unavailable-description text.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/config.py` — add the `memory_pressure` block to `_DEFAULTS`.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/config.yaml` — add the `memory_pressure` block with PSI-specific comments; fix the misleading "Memory Pressure" heading over `memory_usage`.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/SKILL.md` — metric table line-selection column, `some`/`full` semantics, threshold provenance, degradation rule.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_metrics.py` — replace `TestReadProcPressure` fixtures with verbatim PSI samples; add line-selection, unparsable and missing-line cases; extend the `collect_metrics` pressure assertions.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_config.py` — defaults + override coverage for `memory_pressure`.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVIPKT8L0070OVC** (ContextHub) — source item for this migration; superseded by this item and deleted afterwards.
- **WL-0MVI8YM07002Z9VY** (ContextHub, open) — machine-hygiene threshold miscalibration for multi-agent hosts (process/thread/swap); same discovery session, adjacent calibration concern.
- **WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ** (ContextHub, open) — duplicate proposed-actions table/actions; same discovery session, independent defect.
- **SA-0MVLJAG3P0053RJ2** (this repo, open) — recalibrate `cpu_pressure`/`io_pressure` thresholds now that parsing works; deliberately split out of this item's scope.
- **SA-0MUVNZ2QV000LFI9 / SA-0MUVNZ0NU008DTHK / SA-0MUVNZ059002C9Q8** — completed ruff chop items touching `test_metrics.py` / `metrics.py`; no functional overlap, but they explain recent line-number churn.
- **Automated report** — see the "Related work (automated report)" section (retained separately).

## Verification

Changed-scope tests run through the test skill (`/skill:test`), not ad-hoc `pytest`; AC7 additionally needs one real `scripts/evaluate.py` run on a PSI-enabled host.

## Migration note

Migrated from ContextHub `WL-0MVIPKT8L0070OVC` after intake Q1 resolved that the fix belongs in this repo (the only git-tracked copy, and the one `install_pi.sh` publishes globally). The source item is deleted once this item exists, so this item is the single source of truth. Discovery: `discovered-from:machine-hygiene-session-2025-10-21`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Where does the fix land (and therefore where is it tracked)?**
  - Options: (A) SorraAgents `skill/machine-hygiene` with a new `SA-` item; (B) new copy at `ContextHub/skill/machine-hygiene`; (C) patch `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene` by hand.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **A** — fix here, and delete the source `WL-` item once the `SA-` item exists. **Recommended:** A — the fix must be tested where the code is maintained; A is the only option that is durable and reachable by `/skill:machine-hygiene`.
  - Evidence: `diff -r skill/machine-hygiene ~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene` is empty; `SorraAgents/scripts/install_pi.sh` symlinks `$HOME/.pi/agent/skills` → `$SRC_DIR/skill`; precedent for cross-repo tracking: ContextHub `WL-0MQEF8XYR0007BPS` closed against a SorraAgents commit.
- **Q2: `some` vs `full` line per metric?**
  - Options: (A) cpu→`some`, memory/io→`full`, documented; (B) `some` for all three; (C) `full` with fallback to `some` when absent.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **A**. **Recommended:** A — matches kernel semantics (cpu exposes no `full` line) and `full` is what makes memory/io actionable.
  - Evidence: `/proc/pressure/cpu` on this host emits only a `some` line; memory and io emit `some` + `full`.
- **Q3: `memory_pressure` threshold wiring (AC5)?**
  - Options: (A) own `memory_pressure` block in `config.yaml` + `_DEFAULTS`, PSI-calibrated (warning 5 / critical 20); (B) keep sharing `memory_usage` 80/95 with justification comments; (C) own block seeded with 80/95.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **A**. **Recommended:** A — usage % and stall % are not comparable; 80/95 on the `full` line would leave the metric permanently green, restoring the original loss of signal.
  - Evidence: current `pressure_specs` maps `memory_pressure` → `memory_usage`; `config.yaml` has no `memory_pressure` section although `SKILL.md`'s metric table implies one.

No open questions remain.
- **Planning session (2026-10-25, `herdr-downtime`):** no new questions asked — the intake Appendix above already answers Q1–Q3 and no open questions remain.

# Intake Brief — Drive epic children in interactive Herdr panes

## Problem statement

`implement.py drive <parent>` (`phase_drive`, SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9) runs each
child's fresh Pi session as a **headless subprocess**:

```
pi -p "/skill:implement <child>" --approve --no-extensions
```

with `capture_output=True`. The operator therefore has:

- no view of the child session while it runs (only the parent's own progress
  lines and `wait_for_job` heartbeats);
- no ability to watch the agent work, scroll its transcript, or intervene when
  it stalls, hits an approval/question boundary, or loops;
- no evidence after a failure beyond a 5-line `_tail_lines(...)` summary of
  captured stderr/stdout;
- no per-child terminal artefact to point at during review.

An operator running an epic in Herdr already watches a grid of interactive
`π` TUI panes for other work. Drive should produce the same kind of pane —
one interactive Pi TUI session per child, opened as a sibling pane in the
caller's tab — so the epic runs *visibly*.

A headless-in-a-pane variant (option A: `pane split` + `pane run` +
exit-sentinel) was evaluated and rejected as insufficient: it shows log text,
not a browsable/typeable Pi TUI session, and offers no session-level state.

## Users

- **Operator / producer driving an epic from a Herdr-managed Pi session.**
  - *User story:* "As an operator, when I run `implement.py drive <epic>`, I
    want each child implemented in its own interactive Pi TUI pane inside the
    tab I invoked from, so I can watch progress, scroll the full transcript,
    and step in if a child stalls — without leaving my own session."
- **Reviewer / auditor.** *User story:* "As a reviewer, I want each child's
  session transcript to still be inspectable after drive finishes, so I can
  check what the agent actually did."

## Goal

`implement.py drive <parent>` opens **each** child's implementation session as
an interactive Pi TUI agent in a new pane split from the calling pane (same
tab), drives that pane's lifecycle to completion, and continues the existing
serial/blocking-order/parent-last loop — preserving session isolation,
worktree isolation, error isolation, and the recursion guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Pane-per-child in the caller's tab.** For each startable child, drive
   runs `herdr pane split` from the invoking pane (no `tab create`, no
   `workspace create`) with `--cwd <child worktree>` and returns the new pane
   id from `.result.pane.pane_id`; the child Pi TUI is started in that pane via
   `herdr agent start <name> --kind pi --pane <id> -- --approve
   --no-extensions` and prompted with `/skill:implement <child_id>` via
   `herdr agent prompt ... --wait`. Verified by a test that asserts the herdr
   CLI invocations (split/prompt/wait/close) and asserts no tab/workspace
   creation call is made.
2. **Driver waits on session state, not process exit.** Completion of a child
   is determined by (a) `herdr agent wait <name> --until done|blocked` for the
   pane-side signal and (b) the existing `phase_parent` re-read of the work
   item's stage as the authoritative signal. Drive never assumes an
   interactive agent process exits when the work item completes. Tests cover
   the `done`, `blocked`, and timeout transitions.
3. **Blocked children are reported, not silently abandoned.** When an agent
   reports `blocked` (approval/question UI), drive stops the chain, records the
   child id and the pane id in the JSON report (`blocked_child`,
   `blocked_pane`), leaves the pane open for the operator, and emits actionable
   text naming the pane. Tested with a fake herdr runner.
4. **No orphaned sessions:** a pane created by drive is either (a) closed once
   its child reaches a terminal stage and the child's session was clean, or
   (b) explicitly retained and reported (blocked/failed) — never leaked
   silently. Unit tests assert a close call per successful child and no close
   call for blocked/failed children.
5. **Opt-in with fail-open fallback.** Pane driving activates only when
   Herdr is detected (`HERDR_ENV=1` and a resolvable herdr binary) **and** the
   operator opted in (`--pane-sessions`, or `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_PANE_SESSIONS=1`).
   Otherwise the existing `_default_session_spawner` headless path is used
   unchanged. Tests cover herdr-absent, opt-out, and herdr-present paths.
6. **Environment isolation is preserved for pane children.** The child process
   receives `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1`, `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH=<worktree>`,
   and does **not** inherit `PI_SESSION_ID` / `PI_SESSION_FILE` from the
   driving session (assert the constructed env / pane-split `--env` args and
   the `env -u` prefix). Recursion guard and per-child worktree enforcement
   continue to work inside the pane.
7. **Timeouts and iteration bounds are enforced across the new transport.**
   `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_CHILD_TIMEOUT` (and the existing per-child session bound
   `--max-child-sessions`) still bound the wait; a timeout closes the pane,
   records `reason`, and stops the chain as today. Tested with a fake clock /
   fake herdr wait returning `timeout`.
8. **Focus behaviour.** Default is `--no-focus` so the caller's focus is
   unchanged; an explicit `--focus` variant switches to each new child pane.
   Assert the flag passed to `pane split` in both modes.
9. **Report parity.** Human and `--json` reports keep the existing shape and
   gain `pane_id` per driven child plus `transport: "pane" | "headless"`; the
   final summary lists panes retained for inspection. Tests assert the new
   fields and that existing fields are unchanged (no breaking change for
   consumers of the drive report).
10. **Docs.** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (drive section) and
    `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 6.1 document: pane-per-child behaviour, the
    opt-in flag/env var, focus behaviour, blocked-child handling (which pane to
    look at, and that it is intentionally left open), and the headless fallback
    for non-Herdr/automated callers.
11. **Build, tests, and full suite.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit;
    the dev-push full-suite gate is green.

## Design sketch (non-binding)

- Add `_pane_session_spawner(child_id, worktree_path, timeout, env, verbose)`
  next to `_default_session_spawner`, returning the same
  `{"success", "returncode", "reason"}` shape plus `pane_id`.
- Extract herdr CLI calls into a small injectable helper (reuse the fail-open
  style of `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`; do not duplicate its `HERDR_BIN_PATH`
  resolution logic — reuse or import it) so tests fake the CLI boundary with
  no live Herdr.
- In `phase_drive`, select the spawner by transport: existing injection point
  (`spawn_session`) already allows tests to bypass either; the CLI path chooses
  pane vs headless from the opt-in + detection check.
- Agent naming: `drive-<child-id-lowercased>` (herdr names must match
  `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`, unique among live agents) — truncation/validation
  must be tested.
- Pane labelling: on completion/failure, set the pane title via the existing
  `herdr_pane.update_pane_title(status, pane_id=...)` helper so the retained
  pane carries its verdict.

## Constraints

- Do not change the session-per-child rule (SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52), worktree
  isolation, dependency ordering, or parent-advanced-last semantics — all live
  above the spawner.
- Do not change `_default_session_spawner` behaviour for automated callers
  (downtime worker, audit dispatch, CI): headless `pi -p` must remain the
  default outside Herdr.
- No edits to the repo-external Herdr agent skill or the installed
  `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` files (herdr-managed).
- `herdr agent start` requires the pane to be at an interactive shell prompt;
  the implementation must handle `agent_not_ready` (retry within the existing
  timeout or fail with a reported reason), not crash.
- Herdr CLI failures must be fail-open at the boundary (recorded reason,
  chain stops cleanly) — never leave the epic in an unrecoverable state.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Loss of the process-exit completion signal.** An interactive TUI session
  does not exit when the work item completes, so completion must come from
  wl stage + `agent wait`. *Mitigation:* AC 2 makes `phase_parent` the
  authority (it already is) and `agent wait` only a fast-path; covered by tests.
- **Pane/session leakage.** Panes and interactive agents persist after drive
  ends. *Mitigation:* AC 4 explicit close-or-report rule, plus pane-title
  verdict marking for retained panes.
- **Serial drive + visible panes can be noisy.** One pane open at a time,
  closed on success. *Mitigation:* documented; failure/blocked panes retained
  deliberately.
- **Herdr API drift** (JSON shapes, kind list, name rules). *Mitigation:*
  single injected helper for CLI calls; parse ids defensively; fail open.
- **Approval prompts could block an unattended epic.** *Mitigation:* start
  with `--approve` and treat `blocked` as an explicit, reported stop (AC 3).

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive`, `phase_parent`,
  `_child_session_env`, `_default_session_spawner`, `_resolve_child_session_timeout`,
  `_resolve_pi_bin`, `_emit_phase_report`; `--max-child-sessions` and
  `--child-timeout` CLI flags; `spawn_session` injection point.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — deterministic orchestration tests with
  `ScriptedParent` / `RecordingSpawner`; `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py`
  — spawer/env tests.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — fail-open Herdr CLI helper (`HERDR_BIN_PATH`,
  `pane list`/`pane rename`, status prefix/truncation, `update_pane_title`).
- Herdr CLI surface (verified against the installed binary): `pane split
  --current --direction right|down --cwd --env --no-focus`, `pane run`,
  `pane wait-output`, `pane read`, `pane close`, `pane rename`,
  `agent start <name> --kind pi --pane <id> [-- args]`, `agent prompt
  <target> <text> --wait [--until] [--timeout]`, `agent wait`, `agent get`,
  `agent list`, `agent read`. Caller context env: `HERDR_ENV`,
  `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`.

## Appendix: decisions from the discovery conversation

- Transport choice: **option B** (interactive Pi TUI agent in a pane) over
  option A (headless `pi -p` run in a pane, exit-sentinel + `pane read`).
  Rationale recorded: option A shows log text only; B gives a browsable,
  typeable session and Herdr's lifecycle states, at the cost of replacing the
  process-exit completion signal with wl-stage + `agent wait` (AC 2).
- Opt-in rather than default: automated callers (downtime worker, audit
  dispatch, CI) have no Herdr and must keep the headless path (AC 5).
- Forked-decision for planning: whether to factor the herdr CLI boundary into a
  shared module (`skill/shared/`) or keep it local to `implement.py`; prefer
  reuse of `herdr_pane.py`'s resolution/fail-open conventions either way.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9** — implement skill: drive all epic children to
  completion (fresh session per child) — the headless drive this item extends.
- **SA-0MUWBHEEF002A6BO** — When running implement on a parent item implement
  all children — original one-invocation drive requirement.
- **SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52** — When implementing an epic start a new session for
  each child — session isolation rule that must be preserved.
- **SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA** — User-visible progress feedback during long-running
  waits — related observability work for drive runs.
- **SA-0MTFLQEQQ0083EW1** — Update pane title with status emoticon on skill
  completion — reuse `herdr_pane.update_pane_title` for retained panes.

Discovered while implementing SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN (drive timeout reconciliation).

Problem: when implement.py start runs from inside an already-existing worktree (the resume path used by every driven child session), Step 9 writes ImplementState.repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve()) — the worktree path, not the main checkout. phase_finish then calls _remove_worktree(worktree_path, repo_root=state.repo_root) whose safety gate 1 refuses when resolved_path == repo_root (CRITICAL: REFUSE to remove the repository root ... This is the main working tree, not a worktree; Restored status=open).

Impact: every driven child leaks its worktree, finish exits non-zero and restores the item to open even though the commit was pushed — a false failure needing manual status fix; .worklog/worktrees accumulates orphans.

Expected: phase_start should persist the main checkout root (e.g. via _main_checkout_for(worktree) following the gitdir) so phase_finish can remove the worktree after a successful push.

Evidence: SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK finish (commit b11d0877d pushed to dev, finish reported failure, worktree left in place).
data.title: implement.py finish refuses to remove a resumed worktree because phase_start stores the worktree as repo_root

data.description:
# Worktree `@worklog/shared` resolves to the main checkout's stale `dist`

## Problem statement

In an `implement.py` worktree, every `@worklog/shared` import (tests, `src/**`,
spawned CLI subprocesses) resolves through the worktree's `node_modules`
symlink to the **main checkout's** `packages/shared/dist`, so a branch that
changes `packages/shared/src/**` is invisible to the build/test gate: correct
new code fails the gate (false red — observed in ContextHub
WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO) and a genuinely broken shared change can pass (false
green).

## Users

**Primary:** agents (and the humans reviewing their work) running the implement
workflow in a worktree of a repo with a workspace package that is consumed by
path (ContextHub's `packages/shared` is the reference case).

- As an agent implementing an item that touches `packages/shared/src/**`, I
  want the sanctioned gate to exercise the code in my worktree, so a green
  result means my change is correct and a red result names my change.
- As a producer reviewing an `in_review` item, I want the gate result in the
  work-item record to be trustworthy — not a false green, not a false red.
- As an agent starting a fresh worktree, I want the supported setup to be
  automatic or one documented command, so I neither rediscover the `rsync`
  workaround nor "fix" the symptom by weakening tests.

## Root cause (verified)

1. `implement.py start` symlinks `<worktree>/node_modules ->
   <main-checkout>/node_modules` (`_ensure_node_modules_symlink`,
   SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B), and mirrors nested workspace `node_modules`
   directories (`_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`, OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT).
2. `<main-checkout>/node_modules/@worklog/shared` is itself a relative symlink
   `../../packages/shared` — the **main checkout's** shared package.
3. `packages/shared/package.json` `main`/`exports` point at `./dist/*.js`
   (gitignored build output).
4. `npm run build` (or `build:shared`) inside the worktree rebuilds the
   **worktree's** `packages/shared/dist`, which nothing in the worktree
   resolves to; only `packages/shared/src/*.test.ts` (relative imports) see the
   change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Worktree-local resolution.** After `implement.py start` (and after any
   refresh step it performs), `@worklog/shared` resolves to
   `<worktree>/packages/shared` — verified by an automated test asserting the
   resolved package root, and end-to-end by a probe change in a fresh
   worktree's `packages/shared/src/**` that the sanctioned gate
   (`run_tests.py --type full --scope full`) observes and an unmodified main
   checkout would not.
2. **Link-farm `node_modules`.** The worktree's `node_modules` is a real
   directory of per-entry symlinks into the main checkout's `node_modules`
   (nested scopes materialised per package, `.bin` linked as a whole), with
   `@worklog/shared` overridden to the worktree's workspace package. The step
   is idempotent, refreshable when the main checkout's dependency set changes,
   and reported in the `start` JSON report.
3. **No cross-checkout contamination.** No writes pass through the
   `node_modules` symlink into the main checkout's `node_modules`; the main
   checkout stays git-clean apart from gitignored build artefacts after
   start → build → gate → finish from a worktree. The main checkout's own
   build/test behaviour is unchanged.
4. **Hard-fail on stale resolution.** `implement.py finish` (build → test gate)
   fails with an actionable message naming the stale
   `<main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist` path when the worktree changes
   `packages/shared/src/**` while `@worklog/shared` still resolves outside the
   worktree — covered by a test for the detection helper and by a
   negative-path test that the gate cannot silently pass on the main checkout's
   `dist`.
5. **Constraint honoured.** The documented ban on `npm install` inside a
   worktree stays in force and the fix does not require installing into the
   worktree; the option of `rsync`-ing the worktree's shared `dist` into the
   main checkout is explicitly rejected (it mutates the `dist` that the live
   `wl` CLI and every concurrent worktree execute — the WL-0MQRBT8BS00355AB
   class of incident).
6. **Documentation.** The implement skill's worktree section
   (`skill/implement/SKILL.md`) and `implement.py` docstrings describe the
   link-farm resolution order, the refresh/re-run command, the stale-resolution
   failure signature (e.g. the "spy never called" false red), and the
   prohibition on `npm install` in worktrees.

## Constraints

- **Repository:** implementation lives in SorraAgents (`skill/implement/`):
  `implement.py` (`_ensure_node_modules_symlink` ~L1638,
  `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` ~L1735, `run_build`/finish build step
  ~L4432, `finish` gate) and `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (~L547–558).
- **Do not install into worktrees.** `npm install`/`npm ci` inside a worktree
  is forbidden: writes would pass through the symlinked tree and corrupt the
  shared install.
- **Do not mutate the main checkout's `dist`.** Refreshing
  `<main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist` from a worktree changes what the live
  `wl` CLI and all other agents execute, and lets concurrent worktrees clobber
  each other; a lock does not make it safe, only slower.
- **Cross-platform:** the current symlink step is POSIX-first; if linking
  directories on Windows needs junctions, follow the precedent in ContextHub's
  `packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs` (junction on Windows, relative
  symlink elsewhere) and keep the failure non-fatal there.
- **Never weaken tests** to make the gate pass; the false red must be fixed in
  tooling, not by reducing assertions (the exact temptation recorded in
  WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO).
- **Fail-open vs fail-closed:** the *link step* stays non-fatal (usable
  worktree on tooling edge cases); the *staleness detection* in `finish` is
  fail-closed once the worktree diff touches shared source.
- Behaviour change is confined to worktree setups; the main checkout path is
  byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Existing state

- The `node_modules` auto-symlink and its verification are documented in
  ContextHub `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md`
  (WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2): the symlink fixed missing-`node_modules` failures but
  introduced this resolution hop.
- ContextHub `packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs` (`linkSharedPackage()`)
  already replaces a stale packaged copy of `@worklog/shared` with a relative
  symlink to the live workspace package — the same pattern this fix applies at
  the worktree root.
- Current manual workaround (used by WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO): build
  `packages/shared` in the worktree, then
  `rsync -a --delete packages/shared/dist/ <main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist/`
  before running the gate.
- `implement.py` exposes no shared-resolution diagnostic today, and its
  `finish` gate cannot distinguish "shared code changed in this worktree" from
  "shared code unchanged".

## Desired change (decided)

Adopt the **worktree-local link farm** for resolution and **hard-fail** on
stale resolution:

1. Replace `_ensure_node_modules_symlink`'s whole-directory symlink with an
   idempotent link-farm creation: real `<worktree>/node_modules` containing one
   symlink per main-checkout entry, recursively for scopes (`@worklog/*`,
   `@types/*`, …), with `@worklog/shared` pointing at the worktree's
   `packages/shared` (workspace packages are resolved relative to the worktree
   via the `workspaces` field / a small allow-list). `.bin` is linked as a
   whole directory.
2. Keep the existing nested/workspace `node_modules` mirroring behaviour
   unchanged, and keep the whole step best-effort/non-fatal.
3. Add a resolution check: `@worklog/shared`'s resolved package root must equal
   `<worktree>/packages/shared`; expose it in the `start` JSON report and use
   it in `finish`.
4. In `finish`, before the test gate: if the worktree diff touches
   `packages/shared/src/**` and the check fails, hard-fail with the stale
   `<main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist` path and the remediation (re-run
   `implement.py start`/refresh from the main checkout, or run the documented
   refresh command).
5. Update the implement skill docs (worktree `node_modules` section) with the
   new model, the refresh path and the failure signature.

Rejected alternatives: automated `rsync` of the worktree's shared `dist` into
the main checkout (shared-state mutation, live `wl` contamination, concurrency
clobbering); `npm install` in the worktree (forbidden); Node resolution hooks
via `NODE_OPTIONS`/loader or tsconfig `paths` (fragile, uneven coverage across
vitest/tsx/spawned subprocesses); warning-only detection (does not satisfy
AC1).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_ensure_node_modules_symlink` (~L1638) → link farm; `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` (~L1735) unchanged; `run_build` (~L2421)/finish gate (~L4432) → staleness hard-fail; `start` JSON report.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — worktree `node_modules` contract (~L547–558): link-farm model, refresh command, failure signature, `npm install` ban.
- ContextHub `packages/shared/package.json` — `main`/`exports` → `./dist/*.js` (reference case; unchanged).
- ContextHub `packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs` — precedent for live-symlink replacement + Windows junction handling.
- ContextHub `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md` — predecessor verification doc (cross-repo reference only).
- `skill/implement/` tests — new unit tests for the link farm and the staleness helper; extend the finish-gate tests.

## Related work

- ContextHub **WL-0MVLK2JNB002E9JQ** (discovered-from; the intake that produced
  this item — deleted once this item was created, per producer decision).
- ContextHub **WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO** — hit the false-red symptom during the
  persist write-detection work and used the manual `rsync` workaround.
- ContextHub **WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q** — same defect class (stale build artefact
  behind a package resolution) for `packages/herdr`'s packaged copy; its notes
  flag this worktree-isolation gap as tracked separately.
- ContextHub **WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2** / **SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B** — introduced and
  verified the current `node_modules` symlink; this item supersedes that
  resolution model.
- ContextHub **WL-0MQRBT8BS00355AB** — evidence of the blast radius when the
  main checkout's `dist`/`node_modules` is mutated by tooling (why option B is
  rejected).
- **OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT** — nested/workspace `node_modules` symlinks; must keep
  working with the link farm.
- Prior art: ContextHub `packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — link-farm drift.** Entries are materialised at `start`; a dependency
  added to the main checkout later is missing from a long-lived worktree.
  Mitigation: idempotent refresh, called by the resolution check, plus the
  `finish` hard-fail naming the refresh command.
- **Risk — symlink scale.** ~190 top-level entries plus scopes; creation must
  stay fast (sub-second) and must not descend into dependency trees.
- **Risk — Windows.** Directory symlinks may need privileges; use junctions as
  `link-shared.mjs` does, and keep the step non-fatal.
- **Risk — false hard-fail.** A worktree that changes `packages/shared/src/**`
  but intentionally does not rebuild would fail `finish`; the message must name
  the build/refresh command. Mitigation: `finish` builds before the gate, so
  this is only reachable when resolution itself is wrong.
- **Risk — tooling regression for other repos.** The implement skill is used by
  every project; the link farm must degrade to the old symlink behaviour when
  the repo has no workspace shared package, and the detection must no-op.
- **Assumption —** `dist/` stays gitignored in consumer checkouts, so build
  artefacts never dirty the main checkout.
- **Assumption —** agents run the sanctioned gate from the worktree root, so
  `run_tests.py`'s project-root detection targets the worktree.
- **Assumption —** POSIX is the primary platform for implement.py (Linux dev
  hosts); Windows support is best-effort via junctions.
- **Scope-creep watch:** other workspace packages could gain the same
  override; keep the mechanism generic (workspace-aware) rather than
  hard-coding `@worklog/shared`, but do not add per-package features. Any
  further isolation gaps (e.g. ContextHub `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`
  documentation) belong to a separate ContextHub item, not this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: Where should the executable fix live — SorraAgents `implement.py`, a
  ContextHub-local script + implement extension, both, or warning-only?
  **Answer (producer): "A when the SA item has been created delete this [WL]
  one"** — i.e. SorraAgents `implement.py` is the home; the originating
  ContextHub item was deleted after this SA item was created. Source:
  interactive reply in the intake session (`herdr-1792859577-1504585-28248`).
  Prior draft recommendation was (c) both; the accepted answer supersedes it.
- Q2: Which resolution mechanism — worktree-local link farm (A), automated
  `rsync` of shared `dist` into the main checkout (B), or detection +
  actionable warning only (C)? **Answer (producer): "A"** — link farm. Source:
  same reply. Rationale recorded: no shared-state mutation, per-worktree
  isolation, covers vitest/tsx/spawned subprocesses.
- Q3: Should `implement.py finish` hard-fail (not merely warn) when the
  worktree changes `packages/shared/src/**` while `@worklog/shared` still
  resolves outside the worktree? **Answer (producer): "A"** — hard-fail.
  Source: same reply. Rationale: makes false-green impossible; AC4 encodes it.
- Duplicate-work check performed (`wl search "worktree shared dist node_modules
  symlink"` in ContextHub, 15 hits reviewed; `wl search "packages/shared dist
  stale worktree build"` in SorraAgents, no hits): no duplicate. The closest
  items (WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q herdr packaged copy; WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2
  missing-`node_modules`) are completed and do not satisfy this item's ACs.
- Research (verified in the intake session): the resolution chain
  `<worktree>/node_modules -> <main>/node_modules/@worklog/shared ->
  <main>/packages/shared` and `package.json` `main`/`exports` → `./dist/*.js`;
  `implement.py` `_ensure_node_modules_symlink`, `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`,
  `run_build`, `finish`; the implement skill's "do NOT `npm install` in a
  worktree" contract; ContextHub `vitest.config.ts` worktree exclusion;
  `packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs` precedent; ContextHub
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` is missing while `AGENTS.md` links to it
  (routed to a separate ContextHub documentation item).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B** – Auto-symlink node_modules into implement worktrees (implement.py start) (completed)
- **SA-0MVEJIRZ60017H4V** – Unify test-cache namespace across worktrees and the main checkout (open)
- **SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2** – Enforce git worktree usage for all implementation work (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0msgs763c006sm1b, ac1, ac4, acceptance, accepted (+352 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: ac1, ac4, acceptance, accepted, acs (+322 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0msgs763c006sm1b, 0mufg3pja00379ct, ac1, ac4, actionable (+317 more)

Discovered by a full-project `/skill:refactor` scan of this repository (499 source files, clean `dev` checkout).

## User Story

**As a** producer running a refactor scan,
**I want** the report's "Auto-fixed" count to reflect changes actually written to disk,
**so that** I can trust the report and do not believe lint debt was cleaned when the tree is
byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Observed behaviour

`python3 skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` (no work-item id) reported:

```
Auto-fix applied 9 fixes via linters on 437 files
Auto-fixed:     9
Remaining smells: 9
```

but `git status` showed **no** source-file changes (only a pre-existing modification to
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`), and a follow-up check confirmed the same 9 diagnostics
are still present:

```
$ ruff check --select SIM102,EXE005,ISC004,SIM115,UP031,SIM117,EXE001 \
    skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py skill/implement/scripts/implement.py \
    skill/shared/tests/test_wait_for_job.py skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py \
    tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py
Found 9 errors.
No fixes available (3 hidden fixes can be enabled with the `--unsafe-fixes` option).
```

The same 9 findings are then also listed under "Remaining smells (non-auto-fixable)", i.e. they are
counted twice: once as fixed, once as outstanding.

## Root cause (suspected)

`_parse_ruff_fix_output()` in `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` turns **every** JSON entry emitted by
`ruff check --fix --output-format json` into a "fixed finding". Ruff's JSON output after `--fix`
contains the diagnostics that **remain** (those it could not or would not fix, e.g. EXE005/EXE001
shebang/exec bit rules and unsafe-fix candidates), not a ledger of applied fixes. Findings with a
null `fix` field should not be counted as applied.

`_parse_eslint_fix_output()` should be checked for the same assumption.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_parse_ruff_fix_output()` / `_parse_eslint_fix_output()` count a finding as fixed only when the
   linter actually applied a fix (e.g. ruff entry carries a non-null `fix` payload, or fixes are
   detected by comparing file content before/after the run).
2. A regression test proves that a linter run over files whose remaining diagnostics are
   non-fixable reports `fixes_applied: false` / `Auto-fixed: 0`.
3. A full-project scan of a clean tree leaves `git status` unchanged **and** reports `Auto-fixed: 0`.
4. The "Remaining smells" list is not a duplicate of the auto-fixed list for the same diagnostics.
data.title: Refactor skill reports unfixed linter diagnostics as applied auto-fixes

## Goal

As the operator reading my daily standup, I want the "Yesterday I completed work on..." section to separate **auto-dispatched** work (the herdr downtime dispatcher ran `/skill:implement`, `/skill:plan`, `/skill:intake`, `/skill:audit`, `/skill:effort-and-risk` without me) from **manually dispatched** work (I asked an agent to do it in a session I started), so I can see how much of yesterday's progress was machine-driven versus operator-driven.

## Current behaviour

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (`generate_report`, ~line 852) builds `yesterday_items` from `fetch_all_completions_in_window(window_start, window_end)` — every `completed`/`in_review` item whose `updatedAt` falls in the 24 h window, in one flat list.
- Both the markdown report and `yesterday_tts` render that flat list; `--json` exposes a single `yesterday` array.
- Nothing in the pipeline distinguishes provenance, so a `wl next`-selected item implemented by the downtime worker looks identical to one I personally kicked off.

## Provenance signal (already exists — do not invent a new one)

The herdr downtime worker already records provenance in two places:

1. **`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`** — bounded JSONL (cap `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES = 100`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`). Each dispatch entry carries `itemId`, `kind` (`intake`|`plan`|`implement`|`audit`|`risk-effort`|`scheduled`), `dispatchedAt`, `cwd`, `title`, `stage`, and post-spawn enrichment fields (`paneId`, `outcome`). `downtime-coordination.log` and `local-route.log` are separate files and must NOT be treated as dispatch markers.
2. **Worklog comment marker** — `buildDowntimeDispatchComment()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, ~line 7951) writes: `Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at <ISO> — running <skill> <itemId> (<title>).` This survives the rolling-log trim.

Classification rule to implement: an item is **auto-dispatched** iff it has a matching live dispatch-log entry (`itemId`, and `outcome` is not `spawn-failed`) **or** a worklog comment containing the `Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at` prefix within/before the window; otherwise **manual**. Items with no detectable marker default to manual (fail-open to the smaller, less confusing bucket) and the default must be documented.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: The markdown "Yesterday I completed work on..." section is split into two labelled sub-groups, auto-dispatched first then manual (or an explicitly documented order), each with a plain-language heading (TTS-friendly, e.g. "Work auto-dispatched by the downtime worker" and "Work I dispatched myself").

- [ ] AC2: Each sub-group is omitted when empty; the section never renders an empty heading. If the entire window is empty, the existing empty-section behaviour is preserved.

- [ ] AC3: `--json` exposes the split without breaking the existing contract: `yesterday_auto`, `yesterday_manual` (+ `_count` fields) are added and the existing `yesterday` / `yesterday_count` / `yesterday_tts` keys keep their current meaning (all items, unchanged ordering) so downstream consumers do not regress.

- [ ] AC4: TTS output (`yesterday_tts` renders) speaks the split in first person, e.g. "Yesterday the downtime worker completed..." / "I completed..."; no IDs, backticks, or ISO timestamps in spoken lines.

- [ ] AC5: Classification is unit-tested with fixtures — (a) item with a dispatch-log entry → auto, (b) item with only a worklog comment marker → auto, (c) `outcome: spawn-failed` entry → manual, (d) item with no marker → manual, (e) item in `downtime-coordination.log` / `local-route.log` only → manual, (f) trimmed/absent log file → falls back to comment markers and never raises.

- [ ] AC6: Read-side failures (missing/unreadable `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, unparseable JSONL lines, `wl comment list` failure) degrade gracefully: the report still renders, the affected items land in the manual bucket, and a warning is logged — the exit code stays 0.

- [ ] AC7: `skill/standup/SKILL.md` documents the new section layout, the provenance rule, the default-to-manual behaviour, and the new `--json` fields.

- [ ] AC8: Existing standup tests (`skill/standup/tests/`) remain green; new tests are hermetic (`--no-sync --no-commit`, tmp worklog dirs, no real `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` reads).

## Out of scope

- Counting/dashboards of auto vs manual ratios (follow-up if wanted).
- Changing how the downtime dispatcher records markers.
- Re-ranking or filtering the Herdr selection list (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 rule stands: the Herdr list stays the sole ranking path; the split is presentational grouping only).

## Risks / notes

- The dispatch log is a **rolling 100-entry** log, so a busy day can trim entries within the 24 h window; the comment marker path is the durable fallback and both must be combined by OR.
- `kind: scheduled` entries are dispatcher-driven (scheduled prompts) and should be counted as auto-dispatch; document the decision.
- Grouping must not change item ordering inside a group (keep `updatedAt` then `id` sort) or `yesterday_count`.

Discovered during: `/skill:standup` run on 2026-10-25 for project Worklog.

# Framework pre-push hook v3 should resolve the global test runner

**Origin:** `discovered-from:OSL-0MVMCP5DT005PIFS` (filed from ContentCreator; that item was deleted once this one existed and was synced).

**Headline:** The framework's v3 pre-push hook refuses every `dev`/`main` push unless the pushed repo ships its own `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, so `install_pi.sh` still ships a gate-less v2 hook to every project without one. Make v3 resolve the runner local-then-global (the pattern the same file already uses for the context-budget gate), ship v3 everywhere, and upgrade stale installed copies.

## Problem statement

Only the SorraAgents checkout contains `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`; every other project receives its skills from the global install at `~/.pi/agent/skills`. The v3 hook's full-suite gate looks for the runner at `$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` only, so in every non-SorraAgents repo the gate hard-fails (`exit 1`) on any push to `dev`/`main`. `scripts/install_pi.sh` works around that by installing `.githooks/pre-push.v2` — a hook **without** the full-suite gate — into every project that lacks a repo-local runner. The result is two hook variants, and the documented "a red tree is never pushed" guarantee is absent from every project except SorraAgents itself.

The cost is visible: `OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` had to hand-write a local-then-global runner lookup into ContentCreator's hook (its only deviation from the framework's) before the full-suite push gate could be restored there.

## Users

- **Agents pushing to `dev`** in any framework project — they need the same push-time guarantee everywhere, not only in SorraAgents.
- **The operator / producer** — one hook to audit, one documented contract, no per-repo fork to drift.
- **Project maintainers running `install_pi.sh`** — a fresh install must not choose a weaker hook, and a stale installed hook must not silently keep the weaker one.

Example user stories:

- As an agent pushing to `dev` in a project with no repo-local `skill/` tree, I want the full suite to run through the global runner, so a red tree is refused before it reaches the shared branch.
- As a maintainer, I want `install_pi.sh` to install one hook for every project, so I never have to reason about which variant my repo received.
- As the operator, I want an incomplete install to refuse the push and name the bypass, rather than silently skipping the gate.

## Desired change

1. **Runner resolution (v3 hook).** Resolve the runner local-then-global inside the full-suite gate, mirroring the context-budget block in the same file:
   - `$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` when present;
   - else `$HOME/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`;
   - when neither exists, fail closed and name `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` (unchanged fail-closed stance, better message).
   This makes the framework hook converge with the block ContentCreator already runs (`OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` AC2), so the project copy can eventually be deleted rather than forked.
2. **One hook variant.** `scripts/install_pi.sh` installs the v3 hook in every project — the `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` precondition is dropped and `.githooks/pre-push.v2` is removed (or reduced to a pointer note), with the hook-selection comments and `docs/dev/context-budget.md` corrected to describe reality.
3. **Installed-hook upgrade.** `install_pi.sh` must no longer leave a stale installed `.githooks/pre-push` in place forever: when the file's revision marker is a framework revision older than the current one **and the file is an unmodified framework copy**, replace it (backup the previous file, report what happened); when the file carries local modifications, report it and leave it alone. Re-running is idempotent (no rewrite when already current).
4. **Documentation.** The hook contract, the runner resolution order, the revision markers and the upgrade path are documented in the framework docs (`docs/dev/context-budget.md`, plus a hook section or `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` mirroring the project-side doc), and the hook header comment states the resolution order.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Global runner resolution:** with no repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` but a global `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, a `refs/heads/dev` push through the v3 hook executes the global runner with `--scope full --strict-git-env` from the pushed repo's root, and a green run permits the push (regression test, fake global runner).
- [ ] **Fail-closed unchanged:** with neither runner present, the hook exits non-zero on a `dev`/`main` push and names `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`; feature-branch pushes and `refs/worklog/data` pushes still do not invoke the gate.
- [ ] **Parity with the project hook:** the framework gate block and ContentCreator's `.githooks/pre-push` gate block (`OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX`) resolve the runner identically — same order, same fail-closed message semantics — asserted by a test that compares the two resolution behaviours (not the whole files, because the Worklog-sync ordering still differs).
- [ ] **One variant shipped:** `install_pi.sh` installs the v3 hook into a project with no repo-local runner (regression test in `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`), and no install path can select a hook without the full-suite gate.
- [ ] **Installed-hook upgrade:** an existing `.githooks/pre-push` carrying an older framework revision marker and no local modifications is replaced (with a backup and a report); a locally modified hook is reported and left untouched; a second run changes nothing.
- [ ] **Upgrade safety:** upgrading a project that previously ran the v2 hook preserves its existing gate behaviour (branch policy, context budget, Worklog sync semantics) — the replaced hook is the framework v3 hook verbatim, and a test asserts the installed file's revision marker and gate blocks.
- [ ] **Testing/validation criterion:** full SorraAgents suite passes with the new tests, including `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py`, `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`, `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`, `tests/test_context_budget_rollout_docs.py`.
- [ ] **Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`docs/dev/context-budget.md`, hook header, install script comments; the project-side `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` is referenced, not edited, since it lives in ContentCreator).
- [ ] **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- ✗ Do not weaken the gate: the missing-runner path stays fail-closed, `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` stays the only bypass, `--scope full --strict-git-env` stays mandatory.
- ✗ Do not change branch-policy, context-budget or Worklog-sync semantics as a side effect of the runner fix.
- ✗ Do not overwrite a hook that carries local modifications (ContentCreator's copy deliberately keeps per-push Worklog sync — `OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` Q3); detect and report instead (see Q4).
- ✗ Framework code is edited in the SorraAgents repo, never from a project worktree.
- ✗ No ad-hoc test runs during implementation; use the test skill.

## Existing state

- `SorraAgents/.githooks/pre-push` (marker `worklog:pre-push-hook:v3`): branch policy → context-budget gate (local-then-global `measure_context.py`) → single stdin capture loop → full-suite gate (`runner="$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py"`, hard `exit 1` when absent) → feature-branch early exit → Worklog sync.
- `SorraAgents/.githooks/pre-push.v2`: same file without the full-suite gate and without the early exit (Worklog sync runs on every push).
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` (~lines 262–310): picks v3 only when `$CURRENT_REPO_ROOT/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` exists, else copies `pre-push.v2`; copies only when `.githooks/pre-push` is absent, so an installed copy is never refreshed.
- `run_tests.py` resolves the project at CLI time via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, so a global invocation is safe as long as cwd is the pushed repo (ContentCreator's hook proves this in production).
- Existing tests: `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py` (behavioural, fake local runner), `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py` (context-budget local-then-global resolution), `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` (v2/v3 selection), `tests/test_context_budget_rollout_docs.py` (doc/hook comment assertions).
- ContentCreator's hook already implements the target resolution and failing-test reporting; it is the reference implementation, differing from framework v3 only in that deviation plus the retained per-push Worklog sync.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/pre-push` — full-suite gate: add local-then-global runner resolution mirroring the context-budget block; improve the missing-runner message; bump the revision marker.
- `.githooks/pre-push.v2` — remove (single-variant install), or convert to a deprecation note if a test depends on its presence.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — drop the runner precondition, always install v3, add the revision-marker upgrade step with backup and local-modification detection, update comments.
- `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py` — add global-runner and neither-runner cases (fake runner injected into a fake `$HOME`).
- `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py` — extend the existing fallback harness to the test runner (or add a sibling test module for it).
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` — install-into-project-without-runner, upgrade-of-stale-copy, local-modification-preserved, idempotence.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — hook contract and variant documentation corrected; runner resolution and upgrade path added.
- `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` (framework) — optional: the framework-side companion to ContentCreator's doc.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (behaviour regression in ContentCreator):** a wholesale overwrite of an existing hook would drop ContentCreator's per-push Worklog sync (framework v3 exits early on feature pushes). Mitigation: overwrite only unmodified framework copies (Q4); report modified ones.
- **Risk (global runner resolves the wrong project):** the global `run_tests.py` resolves its repo from cwd; if the hook ran it from anywhere else, it would test the wrong tree. Mitigation: keep `cd "$repo_root"` (already the case in the project hook) and assert the cwd in the regression test.
- **Risk (install churn):** rewriting hooks on every install produces noisy diffs in every project. Mitigation: revision-marker comparison, no write when current.
- **Risk (scope creep):** ContentCreator's hook fork, the divergent `post-checkout`/`post-merge`/`post-rewrite` hooks, and the release pipeline are out of scope; record as linked items rather than folding them in.
- **Assumption:** this SA item carries the implementation; the `OSL-` origin record was deleted once this item existed and was synced (Q1).
- **Assumption (Q4):** "overwrite existing installed hooks" applies to unmodified framework copies only; locally modified hooks are reported, not clobbered.

## Related work

- `OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` — *Restore the full-suite pre-push gate in ContentCreator* (completed): the project-side fix whose comment filed this follow-up; its Q3 decision (keep per-push Worklog sync) constrains the overwrite.
- `SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM` — *install_pi.sh propagates the SorraAgents-only test gate to non-SorraAgents projects* (completed): introduced the v2/v3 split this item retires.
- `SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG` — pre-push gate duration vs `implement.py` push timeout (cold-cache cost of the gate).
- `SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81` — full suite deferred from finish to the dev-push gate.
- `OSL-0MVKT9LN10097FA2` — finish-gate false green that surfaced the missing push gate.
- `OSL-0MVK2F1Z300996SA` — the item whose `9c88625c` was pushed red.
- `OSL-0MTMS9R58000J613`, `OSL-0MT5Z8AJ7008LCQQ` — earlier pre-push hook defects (non-fatal `wl sync`, author-identity gate).
- `SA-0MUJLT3BH001IPWK` — active pre-push hook vs committed v3 wiring drift (same hook, adjacent defect).
- `SA-0MVB713300020UFB` — migrate pre-push hook fixtures to `git_sandbox` (touches the same test fixtures).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (ownership/location).** Where should the implementation and the tracked item live?
  - Options: (a) create a sibling `SA-` item in the SorraAgents store and delete this `OSL-` item as the origin record; (b) implement in SorraAgents but keep this `OSL-` item as the tracked item; (c) keep it ContentCreator-local.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — repository-boundary rule; matches `OSL-0MVKT9LN10097FA2` → `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2`.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **(a)** — "delete this item when the SA item is created and synced". Implementation: sibling `SA-` item created in the SorraAgents store; this `OSL-` item deleted after both stores sync.
- **Q2 (install_pi.sh scope).**
  - Options: (a) full unification — v3 for every project, drop `pre-push.v2`, overwrite existing installed hooks; (b) runner fallback only, leave the variant selection; (c) runner fallback + v3 for new installs, never overwrite, document a manual upgrade.
  - **Recommended:** (c) — overwriting risked clobbering ContentCreator's deliberate deviation.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **(a)** — full unification, including overwriting existing installed hooks. Consequence recorded in Q4.
- **Q3 (missing-runner behaviour).**
  - Options: (a) fail closed naming `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`; (b) fail open with a warning.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — the documented "a red tree is never pushed" guarantee must not vanish silently.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **(a)**.
- **Q4 (derived from Q2 = a; flagged for producer confirmation).** Overwriting installed hooks conflicts with ContentCreator's deliberate deviation: its hook keeps per-push Worklog sync, while framework v3 exits early on feature-branch pushes (`OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` Q3), and `tests/test_pre_push_hook.py` there asserts sync on feature pushes. Two readings of "overwrite":
  - (i) overwrite unmodified framework copies only (revision marker matches a known framework revision and the file has no local edits); report and skip modified files — **no change to v3's Worklog-sync semantics**;
  - (ii) overwrite unconditionally — requires first changing v3 so feature-branch pushes still sync, i.e. deleting the early exit and updating `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py`.
  - **Recommended:** (i) — satisfies Q2 (stale framework copies are upgraded automatically) without changing documented framework hook semantics or breaking another repo's suite. **Status: assumption recorded in this brief; producer to confirm (ii) if unconditional overwrite is wanted.**

## Related work (automated report)

Generated by `find-related` (SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1); full untruncated report at
`.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1.md`.

### Related work items

- **SA-0MUJLT3BH001IPWK** – Reconcile active pre-push hook with committed v3 (context-budget gate wiring drift) (open)
- **SA-0MVB713300020UFB** – Migrate pre-push hook fixtures to `git_sandbox` (blocked) — touches the same hook test fixtures
- **SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG** – Add rebuild step to implement SKILL.md after git pull (completed) — unrelated, incidental match

> Repository file matches were generic-word noise (the hook's own tests and
> `audit_runner.py`); the curated **Key Files (predicted)** section is the
> useful list. The two open hook items are genuine neighbours, not duplicates.
