## Goal

**As** a project owner scaffolding agent guidance from this repository, **I want** `templates/project-AGENTS.md` to carry the project-level conventions that audits actually enforce, **so that** a new project inherits the two rules that a 2026-10-29 cross-project audit session had to invent on the spot instead of discovering them late.

Discovered-from: `WL-0MVR8EXR6009F05V` (ContextHub) — an epic audit that returned `Ready to close: No` on an acceptance criterion the producer had already decided to accept, and an `implement` run whose push gate did not run the suite the skill documentation says it runs.

## Scope note (read before implementing)

The definite "the template" is taken to mean **`templates/project-AGENTS.md`** — the canonical project `AGENTS.md` seed consumed by `scripts/init_project_agents.py` (see `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md`). That file is deliberately minimal ("reference structure only"), so this item **adds project-level guidance sections, not a copy of the global rules**.

If the intent was instead the framework sources (`skill/audit`, `skill/report`, `skill/implement`) rather than the project template, re-scope this item before implementing — the framework findings are listed at the end as separate, unfiled work.

## Problem

Two conventions were needed during the ContextHub epic and neither is documented for a project owner:

1. **Recording a producer-accepted acceptance-criteria variance.** The producer decided to accept one AC without the last piece of live evidence. The audit runner ignores `wl auditWaiver` entirely (`grep -n waiver skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` → no matches); the *only* way to make an audit score that criterion `adjusted` (non-blocking) instead of `partial` (blocking) is to write the accepted variance into the criterion's own text in the work-item description, resolve the recorded open question, and *additionally* record `wl audit-waive` so the closure guard and `wl doctor audit-gaps` agree. Done that way, the epic audit returned `Ready to close: Yes` with the criterion `adjusted`, a clean Phase 1/Phase 2 (`calls=2 parse_ok=2`). Done any other way it silently stays blocking and the item ping-pongs between implement and audit.
2. **Declaring the project's real push gate.** `skill/implement` and `skill/audit` both state that the dev-push pre-push hook enforces the full suite (`run_tests.py --scope full`). That is true only where the v3 hook is installed: this repository ships `.githooks/pre-push` (v3, with the scope-aware test gate), but a project seeded earlier (ContextHub) still runs `worklog:pre-push-hook:v2`, which enforces branch policy, the context budget and worklog sync **and nothing else**. Green test evidence therefore came from the `implement.py finish` full-scope run, not the hook. A project owner needs to be told to assert this, because the failure mode is silent: pushes succeed and the cached full-suite evidence the audit consumes read-only never exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `templates/project-AGENTS.md` gains a `## Recording an accepted acceptance-criteria variance` section stating the three-step procedure — (a) amend the criterion's text in the work-item description with an explicit "Accepted variance (producer decision, <date>)" clause naming what evidence stands in for the missing evidence, (b) resolve the corresponding open question in the item description, (c) record `wl audit-waive <id> --reason "<why>"` — and explains **why** the description is mandatory (the audit runner scores an AC from its text and ignores `auditWaiver`).
- AC2: The same template gains a `## Declaring your push gate` section telling a project owner to verify which pre-push hook version the project actually runs (`git config core.hooksPath` + the `worklog:pre-push-hook:vN` banner line) and to record the answer in the project's own guidance, so the full-suite evidence an audit consumes is known to exist (or is known to come from `implement.py finish` instead of the hook).
- AC3: `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md` is updated to match — it must describe the template as carrying these two optional guidance sections and stay truthful about the "reference structure only, never a copy of the global rules" constraint; `scripts/init_project_agents.py` output must remain idempotent (re-running never duplicates the reference or the new sections).
- AC4: A test pins the guarantee: emitting a fresh project `AGENTS.md` via `scripts/init_project_agents.py` produces a file containing both new sections, and re-running it is a no-op (`scripts/init_project_agents.py --dry-run --json` reports no change).
- AC5: The two conventions stay project-scoped: no global workflow rule is duplicated into the template (the global layer remains `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` via `scripts/install_pi.sh`), and `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` is re-measured only if the template changes the always-loaded surface.
- AC6: Full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Key Files

- `templates/project-AGENTS.md` — the canonical project `AGENTS.md` seed; the two new sections go here.
- `scripts/init_project_agents.py` — the installer that reads the template (`TEMPLATE_PATH`) and must stay idempotent.
- `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md` — the installer documentation to keep in sync (it quotes the canonical file verbatim, so the quoted block must be updated too).
- `tests/` — wherever the installer's tests live (`grep -rln "init_project_agents" tests/`), for the AC4 pin.

## Constraints

- Do **not** copy global agent rules (workflow, wl lifecycle, coding disciplines) into the template — that duplication was removed by `SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G` and must not come back.
- Project-specific guidance stays project-specific: both new sections are conventions a *project owner* opts into, not new global mandates.
- Keep the installer idempotent and its output deterministic; no new dependency.
- UK English; match the existing Markdown style of the file and its quoted copy in the docs.

## Related findings from the same session (not in this item's scope — file separately if wanted)

1. `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` maps an AC verdict of `adjusted` to `unmet` in its Acceptance Criteria table (it only knows `met`/`unmet`), so a *passing* audit that carries an accepted variance renders as `❌ failed` with an `unmet` row. The report had to be corrected by hand.
2. `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py start` fails (`ERROR: Failed to create worktree …`) when a feature branch with the expected name still exists but its worktree directory was removed; the operator has to `git worktree add <path> <branch>` manually and re-run `start` (which then resumes idempotently).
3. `skill/audit` in-main-slot mode (default) emits `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` child screens that, when unserviced, produce a `Ready to close: No` whose AC rows are all `partial` **and** persist partial child audits that later block the parent — `--no-child-in-main-slot` was the only path that produced a usable report in three consecutive runs.
data.title: Carry the accepted-variance and push-gate conventions into templates/project-AGENTS.md

# implement.py start: nested node_modules symlink blocks submodule init (bootstrap ordering)

**Discovered from:** RISE-0MVRZKINX004HNEE (tce-the-rising implement run, 2026-10-29).

## Problem

`implement.py start` initialises submodules *after* it creates the
`node_modules` symlinks. When a submodule's own root has a `node_modules` in
the main checkout (tce-the-rising's `core` submodule does), the nested-symlink
pass creates `<worktree>/core/node_modules` inside the still-**empty**
submodule directory. `git submodule update --init` then cannot clone into
`core/` and fails:

```
fatal: clone of 'file:///home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine' into submodule path '…/core' failed
fatal: destination path '…/core' already exists and is not an empty directory.
```

Because submodule init failures are deliberately fail-open (SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ
AC2), `start` only logs a warning and the session proceeds with an
**uninitialised submodule**: `npm run build` (`tsc --noEmit`) then dies with
`Cannot find module './core/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin'`,
`@core-engine/SaveLoad`, etc. Every child session in that worktree must
hand-fix the checkout before it can build.

Secondary defect: even after a successful init, the symlink is not ignored by
the submodule's `.gitignore` (`node_modules/` has a trailing slash, which does
not match a *symlink*), so the superproject reports `M core` and the worktree
looks dirty.

## Evidence

- Call order in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (start phase):
  `_ensure_node_modules_symlink` (≈L4608) → `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`
  (≈L4614) → `_ensure_submodules` (≈L4618).
- Observed on tce-the-rising worktree
  `wl-RISE-0MVRZKINX004HNEE-…`: `git submodule status` showed
  `-19f30ac… core` (uninitialised) while `core/` contained only the
  `node_modules` symlink; the first `npm run build` produced ~40 `TS2307`
  errors from the missing submodule.
- Manual fix that worked: `rm core/node_modules && rmdir core`,
  `git -c protocol.file.allow=always submodule update --init --recursive`,
  re-create `core/node_modules`, and add `node_modules` to the submodule's
  `info/exclude` (the trailing-slash pattern in `core/.gitignore` does not
  match the symlink).

## Required change

- Run `_ensure_submodules` **before** the node_modules symlink passes, or make
  the nested-symlink pass skip paths that are inside an
  uninitialised/unchecked-out submodule (a gitlink with an empty directory).
- Make the worktree's `git status` clean after the symlinks are created: drop
  or neutralise the symlink's untracked status (e.g. immediately cover it by
  an exclude entry, or create the nested link only after init and add the
  path to the worktree's exclude).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A worktree whose submodule root has a `node_modules` in the main checkout is
  fully initialised by `start`: `git submodule status` in the worktree shows a
  checked-out submodule (no leading `-`) and the repo's build succeeds.
- Ordering regression test: fixture repo with a local-path submodule plus a
  `<submodule>/node_modules` in the main checkout → after `start`, the
  submodule is checked out at the recorded commit and the worktree
  `git status --porcelain` is clean.
- The fail-open contract is unchanged: a genuinely failing
  `git submodule update` still only logs a warning and does not abort `start`.
- No behavioural change for repos without submodules or without a submodule
  `node_modules`.
- `implement/SKILL.md` submodule section notes the ordering constraint.

## Constraints

- Do not remove the node_modules symlinking feature itself
  (SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B) — only fix its ordering/ignoring relative to
  submodules.
- Keep the change generic; no tce-the-rising / `core`-specific hardcoding.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_ensure_submodules`,
  `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`, start-phase call order.
- `skill/implement/tests/` — ordering/regression test next to
  `test_implement_submodules.py`-style fixtures.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — submodule documentation.
data.title: implement.py start: nested node_modules symlink blocks submodule init (bootstrap ordering)

discovered-from:MS-0MVM7NJF70037YU4

## Problem

implement.py phase_finish calls git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch, commit) with cwd=repo_root — the main checkout, not the worktree whose branch is being pushed. Git runs the pre-push hook with the main checkout as cwd, so run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env computes its cache key (compute_git_state) from the main checkout's HEAD + dirty content, not from the pushed commit.

Consequence: when a green scope=full entry already exists for the main checkout's git state, the gate is satisfied instantly by another tree's result and never executes a suite for the pushed content.

Observed while landing MS-0MVM7NJF70037YU4 (2026-10-29):
- finish pushed bf1fb2921 to origin/dev; the whole finish phase completed in ~7 min wall, and the push/gate step in much less than a full 10-min suite.
- Querying the cache from a checkout of the pushed commit (git worktree add --detach bf1fb2921; run_tests.py --summary --suite all) reported missing (git_state=14300398...) — no full-suite entry existed for it.
- The only recent green scope=full entries were keyed on the main checkout's state (git_state=c3e34f77..., main dev at d23fb4503 plus a dirty .worklog/scheduled-prompts.json), written 15:04-15:09 by an unrelated run — which the hook matched.

## Impact / why it is not the tested change

The pushed tree and the main checkout tree differed in all four files of the pushed commit, so a green main-checkout run is not evidence for the pushed content. A red pushed commit can therefore reach dev whenever the main checkout happens to be green in cache.

## Desired change (options)

1. Push from the worktree with WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 (documented worktree limitation: the hook runs wl sync, which refuses in a worktree) so run_tests.py keys on the worktree HEAD; or
2. pass the pushed commit/tree to the gate explicitly and key the cache on it; or
3. make run_tests.py's cache lookup for dev/main pushes refuse a hit whose git_state was not computed from the pushed tree.

Keep the existing behaviour that a genuinely red suite blocks the push.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A dev push whose pushed tree has no green full-suite cache entry executes the full suite (or refuses the push) rather than reusing a main-checkout entry.
- [ ] Regression test: a green scope=full entry for the main checkout's state does not satisfy the gate for a different pushed commit.
- [ ] The worktree / wl sync interaction documented in skill/implement/SKILL.md remains accurate.

## Evidence

- /tmp/ms-finish.log (finish + push phase), /tmp/ms-rerun.log (full suite run separately at bf1fb2921: 5121 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failures), host 2026-10-29.
- Main-checkout cache entry .worklog/cache/5242612354ca965b6c6724d2d196e432 (git_state c3e34f77...) vs the pushed commit's git_state 14300398... .

# `implement.py parent`/`drive` start children whose status is `blocked` — re-validate the block before starting or skipping

Discovered-from: **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** (tce-main-street) — producer decision Q3 (2026-10-29): *"yes, though it should first check that the block is still valid"*.

## Goal

As an implement agent running an epic, I need `implement.py parent`/`drive` to never start a child that is deliberately `blocked` unless the block no longer holds, so a verification child is not implemented against a prerequisite that has not landed and I am not asked to fabricate its evidence.

## Problem statement

`phase_parent()` classifies children with `_classify_child()` (`implement/scripts/implement.py:874`): terminal → `skip-terminal`, `in-progress` → `skip-in-progress`, **everything else → `implement`**. Status `blocked` therefore falls through to `implement`.

Blocker awareness exists but does not gate the start:

- `_in_chain_blockers()` only considers blockers that are **themselves children of the same parent** (`implement.py:5920-5975`), so a child blocked on anything outside the parent's children set is startable.
- `external_blockers` is populated from outbound `wl dep` edges only (`implement.py:5771-5790`) and is reported as a "coordination note". It is `[]` when the block is recorded in prose instead of as a dependency edge — which is how cross-project blocks are written (`**Blocked by (SorraAgents):** SA-…` in the child description).

**Live evidence (this item's origin):** on 2026-10-29 `implement.py parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` started child `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` — status `blocked`, unblock condition "`SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2` is in `dev`/`in_review`", which was still `open`/`intake_complete` — created a worktree and reported `external_blockers: []`. The child had to be aborted (`implement.py abort`, worktree removed) to avoid producing unverifiable AC evidence.

The inverse failure matters too: a **stale** block must not strand a child forever. Once the blocker lands, the child must become startable again (or its status refreshed) rather than being skipped silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A child whose `status` is `blocked` is never started while its block still holds: `_classify_child()` (or the caller) yields a distinct `skip-blocked` outcome, and the child is reported in `children_processed` with its blocking ids — not started, not `skipped-in-progress`.
- [ ] **Re-validation of dependency-edge blocks:** for a `blocked` child the outbound `wl dep list` edges are resolved; the block is **stale** iff every blocker is terminal (`completed`/`done`/`in_review`) or soft-deleted, in which case the child is startable again (and the stale block is named in the report/log). Any non-terminal blocker holds the block.
- [ ] **Re-validation of cross-project and prose blocks:** blocker IDs declared in the child description's `Blocked by …` line (and/or a machine-readable `externalBlockers` field, whichever is implemented) are collected and surfaced in `external_blockers`; an unresolvable cross-project id holds the block and is reported with an actionable message (id + where to check it), never silently ignored and never silently startable.
- [ ] A block that cannot be validated (no dep edges, no parseable blocker line, unknown status) is treated as **holding** and reported as unvalidated — it must not default to startable.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: (a) `blocked` + open external blocker → not started, reported with ids; (b) `blocked` + blocker now terminal → stale block detected and child started; (c) `blocked` + no resolvable blocker → not started, message names the unresolved id; (d) `drive` propagates the same classification/report fields; (e) existing in-chain sibling ordering, cycles and terminal/in-progress behaviour unchanged (regression cases).
- [ ] Live evidence recorded on this item: re-running `implement.py parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (three `blocked` verification children) starts nothing and reports all three with their `SA-…` blockers.
- [ ] `implement/SKILL.md` "Guards" list gains the blocked-child re-validation rule (stale blocks are re-evaluated, not honoured forever), and the parent-recursion section documents the new report vocabulary.
- [ ] Node and pytest suites green for the changed framework code (run through the test skill / finish gate, never an ad-hoc runner).

## Constraints

- Do not weaken the existing guards: dependency order, cycle fail-fast, "never re-implement terminal children", "never clobber another agent's `in_progress` claim", and `--finalise-stranded` semantics stay as they are.
- No change to `implement.py start`/`finish` single-item behaviour; this is the parent/`drive` fan-out classification only.
- Cross-project resolution must stay fail-open in the sense that an unresolvable id reports clearly and does not crash the phase — it just holds the block.
- Prose parsing must not become the only mechanism: prefer declared dependency edges, and keep the prose path narrowly scoped to an explicit `Blocked by` line.

## Key Files

- `implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_classify_child()`, `phase_parent()` (child classification, `_in_chain_blockers`), `phase_drive()` (report propagation), `wl_dep_blockers()`.
- `implement/scripts/tests/` (or the repo's existing implement test location) — new unit tests for the classification matrix.
- `implement/SKILL.md` — Guards + parent recursion report vocabulary.
- Reference cases: `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` children `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`, `MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO`, `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR`, `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1` (all `blocked`, blockers in prose).

## Related work

- `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T` — introduced `external_blockers` as coordination notes; this item makes them gate the start.

**Headline:** Split the fix into a test-first contract item, three vertical
behaviour slices (classification → prose/cross-project blockers → drive
reporting), a docs item and a live-evidence item, all under this parent, with
every parent AC mapped to a child.

Round 1 (2026-10-30, plan skill, downtime dispatch — **no interactive
producer available**; questions recorded here and flagged for producer review).

- **Q1 — What is the scope of the live-evidence AC (AC6)?**

  (`MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO`, `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR`, `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1`) and one

  `do-not-delegate` (that is `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`, itself `blocked`), so the
  post-fix run will still start that open child — while AC6 as written says the
  run "starts nothing".

  started, all three reported `skip-blocked` with their `SA-…` ids", and report
  the open held child truthfully with a cross-reference to
  `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`; **(B)** widen this item to also gate on
  `do-not-delegate`/assignee holds (overlaps `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`, which is
  already planned and blocked); **(C)** prove the behaviour on a synthetic
  fixture epic in this repo and record the MS run as pending until
  `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876` lands.
  **Recommended:** A — it proves exactly the bug this item owns (a `blocked`
  child is never started) without duplicating the do-not-delegate item, and
  keeps the live evidence honest about what the run did.

  decides whether C6 (`SA-0MVUTD5YF001PLOF`) can be executed at all, and
  whether the MS epic stays held after this fix lands.

- **Q2 — When a block is found stale, should the child's lifecycle status be
  refreshed, or only the start allowed?**
  AC2 says the child "is startable again (and the stale block is named in the
  report/log)"; the Goal paragraph adds "(or its status refreshed)".
  Options: **(A)** start the child and report/log the stale block, leaving the
  `blocked` status to the lifecycle owner (a comment on the child records the
  stale finding); **(B)** also flip the child to `open` via `StatusLifecycle`
  with an audit comment before starting; **(C)** flip to `open` and clear the
  prose `Blocked by` line.
  **Recommended:** A — it never silently erases a producer-set hold, it keeps
  `phase_parent` a reader of lifecycle state rather than a writer of it, and
  `WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82` shows blocked-status writes are unreliable in `wl`.
  **Answer:** **OPEN QUESTION** — directed to the producer. Why it matters: it
  determines whether C2 mutates child status (and therefore whether it needs
  the `StatusLifecycle` audit-comment path).

- **Q3 — Should a cross-project prose blocker be resolved through the sibling
  worklog scan (so a landed external blocker makes the block stale)?**
  `resolve_worklog_flags` already maps an id prefix to its owning project's
  worklog (verified for `SA` → SorraAgents and `MS` → tce-main-street), so
  resolution is technically available without any network call.
  Options: **(A)** resolve cross-project ids through that scan: terminal →
  stale (child startable), non-terminal → holds, and only a genuinely
  unresolvable id holds as unvalidated; **(B)** do not resolve cross-repo —
  every cross-project id holds, and the child's owner must refresh the child
  when the external item lands; **(C)** resolve opportunistically (try the
  scan, fall back to holds) but never cache the result.
  **Recommended:** A — it is what makes the origin epic self-unblocking when
  the three `SA-…` items land, which is the inverse failure the Goal names
  ("a stale block must not strand a child forever"); B leaves three MS
  children stranded forever and contradicts that Goal.
  **Answer:** **OPEN QUESTION** — directed to the producer. Why it matters: it
  changes C3's acceptance criteria (and its tests) materially.

All three questions are recorded on this item as a comment and the item is
flagged `needsProducerReview`. Planning itself is complete and independent of
the answers; only C6 (Q1), the status-refresh behaviour in C2 (Q2) and the
cross-project resolution in C3 (Q3) depend on them.

Discovered during SA-0MVTV8WQ00014DSK (discovered-from:SA-0MVTV8WQ00014DSK).

## Problem

`implement.py finish` performs the dev push with `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch, commit_hash)` (skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:5313), i.e. from the **main checkout**, not the worktree that holds the commit being pushed. The dev-push pre-push hook then runs the full-suite gate with cwd = main checkout, and `skill/test_cache.py:compute_git_state()` fingerprints **HEAD of the main checkout plus its dirty paths** — not the pushed commit.

Consequences:

1. The full suite can be evaluated against local `dev` (and its dirty tracked files) instead of the pushed tree, so a red commit can pass the dev-push gate.
2. Worse, the gate can be served from the test cache for that unrelated state. Observed: the SA-0MVTV8WQ00014DSK push completed in 18 s (commit c34fd7d91 at 19:54:44, origin/dev updated 19:55:02) while a full suite takes ~12 min, and **no cache entry exists for the pushed commit's git state** (clean-state fingerprint 67451abcabf1301b is absent from .worklog/cache). The only recent entries belonged to a concurrent finish (SA-0MVLJXX9J007UZ63, state f23faf0b, 19:38-19:53), so the gate most plausibly reused that result.

The pushed commit was independently verified green at that exact commit (`run_tests.py --scope full` from a detached worktree at c34fd7d91, `cached: false`, pytest 5163 passed / 15 skipped + node 818/818, 0 failures), so this item is about gate integrity, not a broken tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The dev-push full-suite gate evaluates the tree being pushed (the pushed commit), not the main checkout's HEAD/dirty state — e.g. push from the worktree, or run the gate against the pushed commit via a temporary worktree / explicit `--project-root` at that commit.
2. A regression test pins it: a dev push whose committed tree differs from the main checkout's HEAD cannot be satisfied by a cache entry recorded for the main checkout state (assert the gate's cache key / executed state is the pushed commit).
3. Documentation for the dev-push gate (skill/test/SKILL.md, skill/implement/SKILL.md, docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md) states which tree is validated.
4. Full suite green.

## Goal

As an agent running the changed-scope test gate, I want a changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file to select the node suite for that directory, so a JS/TS test edit is actually executed before commit instead of only at the push-time full suite.

## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_is_test_file()` recognises `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `*.test.mjs` and `*_test.mjs` but **not** the repo's dominant node convention `test-*.mjs`. Consequences:

1. A changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file is not classified as a test file, so `map_changed_to_tests()` tries the convention mapping instead (`test_<stem>.py` etc.) and selects nothing.
2. The same filter builds the `all_tests` pool used by import-graph expansion, so `test-*.mjs` files can never be selected there either.
3. Emission of a node command requires a selected `.mjs` path, so no `node --test` command is produced at all.

Verified while delivering SA-0MVTU1WHS002HN1C: editing three test files (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`, `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-check-final-validation.mjs`) produced a changed-scope command containing only `pytest ...` — no `node --test`. 43 of the 44 `tests/unit/*.mjs` files use the `test-` prefix, so the gap covers almost the whole node unit suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `_is_test_file()` recognises `test-*.mjs` (and the equivalent `test-*.js`/`test-*.ts` naming already used by `tests/unit`) as test files.
- A unit test asserts that changing a `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` file selects `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` and causes a `node --test` command to be emitted by the changed-scope command builder (no pytest-only command).
- The selection never invents a path that does not exist (the existing LP-0MTZYRTNF0092JKW existence filter still applies).
- Existing changed-scope selection tests stay green; the full suite stays green.

## Constraints

- Do not widen selection to arbitrary `.mjs` helper files (e.g. `cli-helpers.mjs`); only the test-file naming conventions.
- Keep the single-source-of-truth rule: one filter function, no duplicated naming logic.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`
- `skill/test/tests/`

## Related work

- discovered-from:SA-0MVTU1WHS002HN1C (observed while adding hermetic ship-gate tests).

# Finish gate: timeout, kill and unparsed reasons

Consumer slice of **SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z** (parent AC1, AC2, AC3, part of AC6). Depends on the runner slice: it classifies the facts the runner now emits.

## Goal

`implement.py finish` must tell the agent whether to fix code, raise `timeoutPerCommand`, or wait for a slot — by classifying timeout, kill, unparsed output and slot contention as distinct reasons, each carrying the facts that make the decision obvious.

## Scope

- Extend the gate-reason vocabulary in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: `timeout`, `killed`, `unparsed` alongside the existing `slot_contention`, `test_failure`, `infrastructure`.
- Map the runner's stable codes (`suite_timeout`, `killed`, `unparsed_failure`, `slot_busy`) to those reasons in `_gate_failure_kind`; an outer `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` around the gate run is also `timeout`. Structured failures keep precedence.
- `_gate_failure_message` renders the deciding facts: for `timeout` the configured timeout and elapsed seconds (plus the `timeoutPerCommand` headroom / wait-for-slot remedies); for `killed` and `unparsed` the command, exit code or signal and the bounded output tails.
- The `test_phase` report object carries `reason`, `configured_timeout`, `elapsed_seconds`, `slot_wait_seconds`, `command`, `exit_code` and `signal` when known.
- `_paced_runner` keeps the measured wait (from the existing `on_wait` callback) and surfaces it into the gate result instead of only logging it.
- `unknown` is retained only as a documented last resort, and only with a non-empty detail — never for a timed-out, killed or non-zero run.
- Update `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (gate-failure diagnostics section).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each of timeout, kill, unparsed output and slot contention yields a distinct `reason`, proven by gate-classification unit tests.
- [ ] A run that exceeds `timeoutPerCommand` is classified as a timeout/infrastructure result naming the configured timeout and elapsed seconds, with a stable notice code; it never reports `reason: unknown` with `failures: []`.
- [ ] A run that exits non-zero or is killed with no parsable failures is classified as an unparsed/infrastructure condition carrying the command, exit code/signal and bounded stdout/stderr tails (not an empty `failures` list presented as a code failure).
- [ ] `test_phase` carries `elapsed_seconds` and `slot_wait_seconds` as separate values, with the wait never added to the suite elapsed.
- [ ] Structured test failures still win classification (no genuine code failure is ever reported as infrastructure).
- [ ] `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` documents the new reasons and fields and how to read them.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add the three reason constants and extend `_gate_failure_kind` in code-first order (notice codes before legacy text prefixes).
2. Extend `_gate_failure_detail`/`_gate_failure_message` to render the fact fields per reason.
3. Populate the new `test_phase` keys where the report is built; keep the keys additive for existing consumers.

**Key Files:**
- skill/implement/scripts/implement.py
- skill/implement/tests/test_implement_gate_failure_reason.py
- docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md

## Constraints

- Reporting/classification only: no cache behaviour change, no semaphore widening.
- The finish gate stays changed-scope; the full suite remains the dev-push gate's job.
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- New gate reasons (`timeout`, `killed`, `unparsed`) and fact fields in `implement.py`'s finish report and message.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` gate-diagnostics section updated.
- Green gate-classification tests from the first slice.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by **SA-0MVU8XRBQ000DG9D** (runner facts) — classification consumes the emitted codes and fields.

# Prove queue wait is outside the timeout budget

Verification slice of **SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z** (parent AC3, AC4). Depends on the runner and finish-gate slices.

## Goal

Prove, with a deterministic test, that time spent queued for a host test slot is neither charged to a suite's per-command timeout budget nor hidden inside the suite's elapsed time — and that it is reported as its own duration end to end.

## Scope

- Test that stubs a **blocking slot acquisition** (the slot context manager / semaphore acquire blocks for a controlled interval) and then runs a command whose own runtime plus timeout margin leaves no room for the wait: the command must still succeed, proving the wait was outside the timeout budget.
- Assert the wait is reported as `slot_wait_seconds` and that `elapsed_seconds` covers the command only (wait not folded in).
- Assert the same separation survives aggregation (`run_all`) and the finish-gate report (`test_phase`), including the bounded-wait expiry case where the whole wait duration is reported with the `slot_busy`-style code.
- Keep every interval small (seconds, not minutes) and keep the host semaphore out of it (stubbed acquisition, isolated `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` if a real semaphore is used).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test stubs a blocking slot acquisition and proves the per-command timeout budget is unaffected by the wait.
- [ ] The same test (or a sibling) proves `slot_wait_seconds` and `elapsed_seconds` are reported as separate values at suite, aggregate and finish-gate level.
- [ ] A run that waits for a test slot reports the wait as its own duration, distinct from suite elapsed time, with a stable `slot_busy`-style code, including the bounded-wait expiry path (so "waited then gave up" is distinguishable from "ran and failed").
- [ ] No real multi-minute sleep, no host-wide slot contention introduced by the test.
- [ ] Parent AC4 is covered by a named test referenced from the parent work item.

## Minimal implementation

1. Stub the slot context manager to sleep a controlled interval, recording entry/exit.
2. Run a fast stub command with a timeout just above its runtime; assert success and the reported fields.
3. Add the aggregate and gate-level assertions reusing the existing fixtures.

**Key Files:**
- skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py
- skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py
- skill/implement/tests/test_implement_gate_failure_reason.py

## Constraints

- No `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` change and no bypass of the host semaphore in production code (stubs live in tests only).
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- Blocking-slot test proving wait is outside the per-command timeout budget.
- Suite/aggregate/gate assertions that `slot_wait_seconds` and `elapsed_seconds` are separate.
- Evidence comment on the parent work item naming the test that covers parent AC4.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by **SA-0MVU8XRTE008VDO2** (finish-gate reasons) — the gate-level assertions need the reported fields.

# Docs: classification fields in skill references

Documentation slice of **SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z** (parent AC6). Depends on the runner, finish-gate and queue-wait slices so the documented field names match the shipped code.

## Goal

An agent reading the implement and test skills must be able to interpret every finish-gate `reason` and its fact fields, and know the correct next action, without reading the source.

## Scope

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`: operator/agent-facing guidance on reading `reason` (`timeout`, `killed`, `unparsed`, `slot_contention`, `test_failure`, `infrastructure`) and the fact fields (`configured_timeout`, `elapsed_seconds`, `slot_wait_seconds`, `command`, `exit_code`, `signal`), including the correct remediation per reason (raise `timeoutPerCommand` with headroom / treat as infrastructure / inspect tails / wait a staggered delay).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`: consistent wording and cross-references for the same codes/fields (no divergent names).
- Add a lightweight consistency check (docs-vs-source) so a renamed code cannot silently leave the docs stale.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `skill/implement/SKILL.md` documents each gate `reason`, the fact fields, and the recommended action for it.
- [ ] Both reference docs use the same code/field names as the source constants, with cross-references between them.
- [ ] A check (test or scripted grep with a clear failure message) fails when a documented code/field no longer exists in source, or a source code is undocumented.
- [ ] Content is UK English and consistent with the existing reference-doc structure.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add the classification table + remediation guidance to `skill/implement/SKILL.md`.
2. Align the two reference docs and cross-link them.
3. Add the consistency check next to the existing skill tests.

**Key Files:**
- skill/implement/SKILL.md
- docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md
- docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md

## Constraints

- Documentation and docs-consistency tooling only; no behaviour change.
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` classification/remediation guidance.
- Aligned `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` sections.
- Docs-vs-source consistency check.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by **SA-0MVU8XSGI003DBWR** (queue-wait proof) — documents the final field names and semantics.

# `phase_parent`: classify a still-blocked child as `skip-blocked` (dep-edge re-validation)

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2**. Test-first sibling: **C1** (blocked-child classification matrix).

## Goal

As an implement agent running an epic, I need `implement.py parent` to never
start a child whose `status` is `blocked` while its block still holds, and to
re-evaluate (not honour forever) a **stale** block, so a verification child is
never implemented against a prerequisite that has not landed and a landed
prerequisite never strands its dependent.

## Context

- `_classify_child()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, ~line 1127)
  returns `implement` for `status: blocked`. Precedence today:
  terminal → `skipped-held` → `skip-in-progress` → `implement`.
- `phase_parent()` (~line 6609) builds `classifications` with
  `action`/`external_blockers` and gates the start only on **in-chain**
  blockers (`_in_chain_blockers`, blockers that are themselves children of the
  same parent, ~line 6787). `_next_child_to_implement()` (~line 1227) is a
  second, legacy classification path kept consistent by tests.
- `wl dep list <id> --json` → `outbound` entries with `id` and `status`
  (`wl_dep_blockers`, ~line 565).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `blocked` child whose block still holds yields a **distinct** classification (`skip-blocked`, i.e. `ACTION_SKIP_BLOCKED`) from `_classify_child()` (or its caller); it is never `implement`, `skip-in-progress` or `skipped-terminal`. Precedence is explicit and documented: `skip-terminal` → `skipped-held` → `skip-in-progress` → `skip-blocked` → `implement`.
- [ ] **Dep-edge re-validation:** for a `blocked` child the outbound `wl dep list` edges are resolved; the block is **stale** iff every blocker is terminal (`completed`/`done`/`in_review`, reusing `_is_terminal_status` / soft-delete semantics) — in which case the child is startable again and the stale block is named in the report (a `stale_blocks` entry, and a log/comment line naming the blocker ids). Any **non-terminal** blocker holds the block.
- [ ] `children_processed` entries for a held child carry `action: "skip-blocked"`, the child id, its status and `blocking_ids` (the ids that hold it); the report also lists them in `blocked_children` so `phase_drive`'s existing propagation keeps working.
- [ ] A block that cannot be validated (no dep edges, no parseable blocker line, unknown status) is treated as **holding** and reported as unvalidated (`unvalidated_blocks`) — it must not default to startable. (The prose/cross-project resolution that makes such a child actionable lands in C3; until then the fail-closed behaviour is the correct default.)
- [ ] A `blocked` child with at least one terminal blocker **and** one non-terminal blocker still holds (the non-terminal one wins); a `blocked` child whose blockers are all soft-deleted is stale/startable.
- [ ] `_next_child_to_implement()` (legacy helper, still covered by `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`) applies the same rule so the two classification paths cannot diverge; it is kept, not deleted.
- [ ] Unchanged: dependency order, cycle fail-fast, terminal children never re-implemented, `skipped-held` precedence, `skip-in-progress` never clobbering another agent's claim, `--finalise-stranded` semantics, and single-item `start`/`finish` behaviour.
- [ ] The C1 tests for cases (a), (b) and (e) are green; the changed-scope suite is green through the finish gate (`/skill:test`) and the full pytest + node suite is green at the dev-push gate (parent AC 8).

## Minimal implementation sketch

- Add `ACTION_SKIP_BLOCKED = "skip-blocked"` beside `ACTION_SKIPPED_HELD` (~line 213).
- New helper, e.g. `_blocked_child_state(child, blockers) -> {"action", "blocking_ids", "stale_ids", "unvalidated"}`, called from `_classify_child`'s callers (`phase_parent`, `_next_child_to_implement`) with the child's outbound edges — `_classify_child` itself has no edge data, so either widen its signature with an optional `blockers` argument (defaulting to `None` → unvalidated/fail-closed) or keep the status test in `_classify_child` and resolve the blocked verdict in the callers. Prefer the smallest change that keeps both call sites consistent.
- Extend the `classifications`/`child_results` entries and the "no startable child" message to name the blockers.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken existing guards; do not change `start`/`finish` single-item behaviour.
- Prefer declared dependency edges over prose; no `wl` schema change, no `gh`/network calls.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_classify_child` (~1127), `_next_child_to_implement` (~1227), `phase_parent` (~6609, incl. `_in_chain_blockers` ~6787), `wl_dep_blockers` (~565), `TERMINAL_STATUSES`/`_is_terminal_status` (~1082).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` — C1's matrix (red to green).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py` — existing parent suite that must stay green.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` — existing dependency-order suite that must stay green.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` — parent.
- `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T` — introduced `external_blockers` as coordination notes (superseded here).
- `SA-0MVS1QS9J009DGPT` — the *parent's own* outbound edges / `blocked` status; distinct, do not implement here.
- `SA-0MVO6UL70000HT0J` — terminal blockers still gate topological ordering; distinct.

# Prose `Blocked by` and cross-project blockers hold a `blocked` child

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2**. Depends on **C2** (`skip-blocked` classification); test-first contract in **C1** (case (c)).

## Goal

As an implement agent, I need a blocker that is declared in the child's
description (the cross-project convention) to gate the start exactly like a
dependency edge, so a verification child is never started against an
unlanded prerequisite in another repository and the report tells me which id
to check and where.

## Context

- Cross-project blocks are written in prose, e.g. on
  `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`:
  `**Blocked by (SorraAgents):** \`SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2\` — *Finish gate: …* (in progress; …)`
  followed by an `**Unblock condition:**` line. `wl dep list` on that child
  returns `outbound: []`, so today the phase reports `external_blockers: []`
  and starts it.
- `wl show --children --json` already returns each child's `description`, so
  no extra fetch is needed to parse it.
- Ids in this worklog look like `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` / `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1`;
  ids belonging to another repository's worklog are **not** resolvable from
  this one (`wl show` fails).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A narrowly scoped parser extracts blocker ids from an **explicit** `Blocked by …` line only (case-insensitive, tolerating the bold/labelled form `**Blocked by (SorraAgents):**` and a plain `Blocked by:`); it must not treat arbitrary prose, `Unblock condition:` text or `Related work` ids as blockers.
- [ ] **Re-validation of cross-project and prose blocks:** blocker IDs declared in the child description's `Blocked by …` line are collected and surfaced in `external_blockers` (id + resolvable status, or `unresolved`); an unresolvable cross-project id holds the block and is reported with an actionable message (id + where to check it), never silently ignored and never silently startable. The merged set gates the start via C2's `skip-blocked` verdict.
- [ ] **Resolvable** prose blocker (present in this worklog): terminal → stale (child startable, blocker named); non-terminal → holds, reported with its status.
- [ ] **Unresolvable** (cross-project / unknown) prose blocker → **holds**, and the report/message names the id plus where to check it (e.g. "check the owning project's worklog", with the id's prefix as the hint). Never silently ignored, never silently startable.
- [ ] A `blocked` child with **no** dep edges and **no** parseable `Blocked by` line is reported as **unvalidated** and holds (fail-closed) — never defaults to startable.
- [ ] Parsing never crashes the phase (fail-open on the parser, fail-closed on the verdict): a malformed line yields "unvalidated" rather than an exception.
- [ ] No `wl` schema change and no new machine-readable field: prose + declared dep edges only (the parent AC's "and/or a machine-readable `externalBlockers` field, whichever is implemented" is satisfied by this choice). Cross-project ids are not resolved over the network.
- [ ] C1 cases (c) and the fail-closed case are green; the changed-scope suite is green through the finish gate (`/skill:test`).

## Assumptions (recorded on the parent)

- A cross-project block can therefore never go stale automatically: when the
  external item lands, the child's owner must refresh the child (status
  `open`, or remove/annotate the `Blocked by` line). This is the fail-closed
  behaviour the parent's AC 3 asks for and is recorded as an assumption.

## Constraints

- Prose parsing must stay narrowly scoped (one explicit line); declared
  dependency edges remain the preferred mechanism.
- Do not weaken C2's fail-closed default, existing guards or single-item
  `start`/`finish` behaviour.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — blocked-child state helper from C2, `phase_parent` classification/reporting (~6609), `wl_dep_blockers` (~565), `wl_show_children` (~525).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` — C1 matrix (case (c), fail-closed).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py` — existing parent suite that must stay green.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` — existing dependency-order suite that must stay green.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` — parent.
- `SA-0MVS1QS9J009DGPT` — the *parent's own* outbound edges; distinct.
- `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (tce-main-street) — origin epic whose `blocked` verification children use the prose convention; the live-evidence item `C6` exercises it.
data.title: Prose Blocked by and cross-project blockers hold a blocked child

# `phase_drive`: propagate `skip-blocked` classification and blocker ids

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2**. Depends on **C2** and **C3**; test-first contract in **C1** (case (d)).

## Goal

As a dispatcher running `implement.py drive <epic>` unattended, I need the
drive report to carry the same blocked-child verdicts as `parent` — with the
blocking ids — so no session is spawned for a `blocked` child and I can see
which id to wait for without re-reading the child's description.

## Context

- `phase_drive()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, ~line 7934) loops
  over `phase_parent` reports and spawns a fresh Pi session per startable
  child. It already re-propagates `blocked_children` (ids only) on the
  "no startable child" path (~line 8368).
- After C2/C3 a child can be classified `skip-blocked` with `blocking_ids`;
  drive must not spawn a session for it and must surface the ids.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No session is spawned for a child classified `skip-blocked` by the parent phase; `sessions_spawned` and `children_driven` reflect that (the child is not counted as driven, failed or retried).
- [ ] The drive report carries the blocked verdicts with their blocking ids — `blocked_children` keeps its existing id-list shape **and** the richer per-child entries (child id, status, `blocking_ids`, stale/unvalidated flags) are present, so both existing consumers (`tests/test_implement_drive.py::test_stops_when_no_startable_child`) and new ones work.
- [ ] The "no startable child" message names the blocking ids (not just "blocked or held"), so an unattended dispatcher log is actionable.
- [ ] Existing drive behaviour unchanged: per-child session bound, finish-attempt bound and reset-for-retry recovery, timeout reconciliation (`completed-late`), stranded-child detection, `skipped-held` propagation, recursion guard, and parent-advanced-last.
- [ ] C1 case (d) is green; the changed-scope suite (pytest + node where applicable) is green through the finish gate (`/skill:test`).

## Constraints

- Reporting/loop-control change only — no new spawning policy, no change to
  `parent`'s classification (that is C2/C3) or to single-item `start`/`finish`.
- Do not weaken existing bounds or guards.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` (~7934, report propagation ~8360-8380), `_reconcile_spawn_failure`, `phase_parent` report fields from C2/C3.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — scripted-parent/recording-spawner harness; existing propagation test to extend.
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — recovery behaviours that must stay green.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` — C1 case (d).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` — parent.
- `SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9` — drive: fresh session per child (the loop this extends).
- `SA-0MVQ5AXLF002PAQ3` — `skipped-held` propagation precedent.

# Docs: `implement/SKILL.md` guards + parent-recursion report vocabulary

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2**. Depends on **C2**, **C3** and **C4** (the vocabulary must match the shipped code).

## Goal

As an operator or agent reading the implement skill, I need the Guards list and
the parent-recursion section to state the blocked-child re-validation rule and
the new report vocabulary, so nobody re-learns it from a failed run.

## Context

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` "Guards (deterministic, in `phase_parent`)"
  currently says only: *"**Blocked children wait** — a child is only started
  once every in-chain blocker is terminal; otherwise it is reported in
  `blocked_children`."* and, earlier in the parent-recursion section, that
  cross-project blockers are "coordination notes" (the wording superseded by
  this work, originally from `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T`).
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` documents report fields; extend it
  only where it already enumerates parent/drive report keys.
- `tests/test_implement_skill_doc_hygiene.py` and
  `tests/test_implement_skill_session_per_child_doc.py` enforce doc
  consistency — they must stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `implement/SKILL.md` "Guards" list gains the blocked-child re-validation rule (stale blocks are re-evaluated, not honoured forever), and the parent-recursion section documents the new report vocabulary (`action: "skip-blocked"`, `blocking_ids`, `stale_blocks`, `unvalidated_blocks`, extended `blocked_children` entries). The rule is stated once: a child whose `status` is `blocked` is never started while its block holds; the block is re-validated on every run against outbound dep edges and the explicit `Blocked by …` line.
- [ ] The parent-recursion section documents the new report vocabulary: `action: "skip-blocked"`, `blocking_ids`, `stale_blocks`, `unvalidated_blocks`, and the extended `blocked_children` entries — including that an unresolvable cross-project id **holds** the block and is reported with where to check it.
- [ ] The "cross-project external blockers are coordination notes" wording is corrected to the new contract (they now gate the start) with a pointer to this parent item, so the two statements cannot contradict each other.
- [ ] The `drive` section states that a `skip-blocked` child is never spawned and that its blocking ids appear in the drive report.
- [ ] Precedence of classifications is stated once, unambiguously: `skip-terminal` → `skipped-held` → `skip-in-progress` → `skip-blocked` → `implement`.
- [ ] Doc-hygiene tests green; changed-scope suite green through the finish gate (`/skill:test`).

## Constraints

- Documentation only — no code changes. If the shipped vocabulary differs from
  the wording above, document what shipped and record the difference in a
  comment on this item.
- Keep the edit surgical: no restructuring of `SKILL.md`.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Guards list, parent-recursion report vocabulary, drive section.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — parent/drive report-field reference (extend only if it already enumerates them).
- `tests/test_implement_skill_doc_hygiene.py` — doc guard that must stay green.
- `tests/test_implement_skill_session_per_child_doc.py` — doc guard that must stay green.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` — parent.
- `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T` — the superseded "coordination note" wording.
- `SA-0MVQ5AXLF002PAQ3` — `skipped-held` vocabulary precedent in the same section.
data.title: Docs: implement/SKILL.md guards + parent-recursion report vocabulary

# Live evidence: `parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` starts no blocked child

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2**. Depends on **C2**, **C3** and **C4**. **Do not run until the producer answer to the OPEN QUESTION (Q1) on the parent is recorded** — see "Scope" below.

## Goal

As a producer, I need proof on the real epic that triggered this bug that the
fixed `implement.py parent` starts **no** child whose block still holds and
names each child's blocker, so I can trust the guard on live data rather than
only on fixtures.

## Context

- Origin epic: **`MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6`** in `/home/rgardler/projects/tce-main-street` (worklog auto-resolved from cwd; `SA-…` ids in its children's prose belong to the SorraAgents worklog and are therefore unresolvable there).
- Its verification children on 2026-10-30:
  - `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` — **`open`**, `assignee: Map`, tag `do-not-delegate` (its `blocked` status could not be stored: `WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82`);
  - `MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO` — **`blocked`**, blocker `SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO` in prose;
  - `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR` — **`blocked`**, blocker `SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z` in prose;
  - `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1` — **`blocked`**, blocker `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2` in prose.
- The 2026-10-29 incident: the phase started `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`, created a worktree and reported `external_blockers: []`; it had to be aborted.
- `phase_parent` does **not** honour `do-not-delegate` or an assignee hold (that is `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`, itself `blocked`), so an `open` held child is still startable.

## Scope (set by the producer answer to Q1)

- If Q1 = **A** (recommended): evidence covers the three `blocked` children — none started, all three reported `skip-blocked` with their `SA-…` ids — and the run's treatment of `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` is reported truthfully with a cross-reference to `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`.
- If Q1 = **B**: this item also waits for `do-not-delegate`/assignee-hold gating, and the evidence must show **nothing** started.
- If Q1 = **C**: the evidence is a synthetic fixture epic in this repo, and the MS run is recorded as pending until `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876` lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Live evidence recorded on this item: re-running `implement.py parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (three `blocked` verification children) starts nothing and reports all three with their `SA-…` blockers — per the Q1 scope answer below.
- [ ] Pre-run state captured: `wl show MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6 --children --json` child statuses/assignees/tags recorded on `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` before the run.
- [ ] `implement.py parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` run from `/home/rgardler/projects/tce-main-street` after C2–C4 land, with the full `--json` report pasted on `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2`.
- [ ] The report shows each `blocked` child with `action: "skip-blocked"` and its blocking id(s) (`SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO`, `SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z`, `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2`), and **none of them was started** (no worktree created for them).
- [ ] No child of the epic is left claimed, dirty or with a worktree as a result of this run; if anything was started, it is aborted (`implement.py abort <child>`, worktree removed) and the failure is recorded on this item instead of being worked around.
- [ ] Post-run state recorded and compared with the pre-run state (no unintended mutation of the MS epic or its children).
- [ ] Any deviation from the expected report is raised as a new work item linked to `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2`, not silently accepted.

## Constraints

- Read-only with respect to the MS epic's *work*: the run must start nothing; do not implement any MS child from here (repository boundary — framework code lands in SorraAgents).
- This is a live `implement.py` invocation, not a test run; any test execution still goes through the test skill.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_parent` report under test (the evidence source is the tce-main-street worklog, not a repo file).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` — the fixture-level equivalent of this live check.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` — parent.
- `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` — origin epic (holds `assignee: Map` as a scheduling hold; do not disturb it).
- `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2`, `SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO`, `SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z` — the three blockers.
- `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876` — `do-not-delegate` gating (blocked; the reason `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` is only held by tag/assignee).
- `WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82` (ContextHub) — `wl update --status blocked` reverting to `open`.

# Push to dev from the worktree that holds the commit

Parent: **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3** — the core fix (blocks nothing else, unblocks
the evidence and docs slices).

## Goal

`implement.py finish` must run its dev push from the checkout that has the
pushed commit checked out — the worktree — on the **first attempt and the
non-fast-forward retry**, so `.githooks/pre-push` resolves its
`--project-root` to the pushed tree. Fail closed when that tree cannot be
materialised.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Push cwd is the pushed tree.** `implement.py finish` runs its dev push from
  the checkout that has the pushed commit checked out (the worktree) — for the
  first attempt *and* the non-fast-forward retry — so the main checkout's
  working tree is never the subject of the dev-push gate.
- **Retry path re-establishes the subject.** After the recovery rebase rewrites
  the commit, the retry push has the rebased commit checked out (pushed sha ==
  push cwd `HEAD`), so the hook's `--project-root` is the pushed tree.
- **Fails closed with an actionable message.** A pre-push subject guard refuses
  the push when the push cwd does not hold the pushed commit (worktree gone,
  `HEAD` ≠ pushed sha, dirty state that cannot be rebased): finish raises an
  error naming the **commit, branch, worktree and the actual `HEAD`**, and
  never silently pushes from a checkout holding a different commit.
- **Recovery behaviour preserved.** Push timeout → process-group kill +
  recoverable-state comment; non-fast-forward → fetch + rebase + retry;
  worktree retained until the push succeeds. `_restore_local_dev_after_failed_push`
  and `_sync_parent_branch` still operate on the main checkout.
- **Step 5 stays hygiene only.** The local-dev fast-forward remains a main
  checkout hygiene step (never the gate subject); `repo_root` stays the subject
  of the main-checkout guard and of `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev`.
- **Cache compatibility preserved.** Full-suite evidence stays path-independent
  (`HEAD` sha + dirty-content hash + suite command): pushing from the worktree
  reuses/creates the same audit-acceptable `scope: full` entries, and
  `mirror_suite_cache` still mirrors the worktree cache into the main checkout.
- **Docs/comments in scope.** Code comments and docstrings that assert the old
  behaviour (the Step-5/Step-6 comments claiming the hook measures the main
  checkout, `git_push_to_dev`'s "cwd: worktree root" docstring) are corrected
  in this change set.
- **No weakening.** `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` and friends remain explicit escape
  hatches; the default path never fails open.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — phase_finish Step 6 push call site
  (currently `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch, commit_hash)`),
  `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` retry push, new subject guard +
  `PushSubjectMismatchError`, Step-5/Step-6 comments.
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py`,
  `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` (markers
  removed here).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `_assert_push_subject(push_cwd, commit_hash, branch, worktree_path)`:
   push cwd exists, is a git worktree, and `git -C push_cwd rev-parse HEAD`
   equals `commit_hash` — else raise `PushSubjectMismatchError` naming commit,
   branch, worktree and actual `HEAD`.
2. Step 6: guard, then `git_push_to_dev(worktree_path, branch, commit_hash)`.
   Keep the Step-5 fast-forward and the pre-push main-checkout guard on
   `repo_root`.
3. `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()`: after `git rebase origin/dev`, recompute
   `new_commit` **from the worktree**, guard, then retry
   `git_push_to_dev(worktree_path, branch, new_commit)`; keep the existing
   recoverable-state comments on failure.
4. Leave the ancestry assertion (Step 6a) reading `origin/dev` — it verifies
   what landed, not which cwd pushed.
5. Remove the `xfail(strict=True)` markers from the regression tests.

## Definition of Done

- Change-set tests green (retry cwd == worktree, first attempt cwd == worktree,
  guard refuses a mismatch), and a real `implement.py finish` dev push runs the
  full-suite gate with the worktree as `--project-root`.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (enforced at the
  dev-push gate on the pushed commit).

## Dependencies / Deliverables

- Prerequisite: the regression-test item (test-first ordering).
- Deliverable: `implement.py` push-from-worktree behaviour + guard + corrected
  comments.

# Surface dev-push gate evidence on success

Parent: **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3** — observability slice; makes the gate auditable
and makes the 2026-10-28 68-second anomaly diagnosable.

## Goal

For every `implement.py finish`, make *"the gate ran and hit a cache for commit
X"* distinguishable from *"the gate never ran"* — without weakening the gate and
without executing tests from the pusher.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Gate evidence is surfaced.** Hook/push `stderr` is logged by
  `git_push_to_dev()` on success too (at least INFO/DEBUG) — today it is
  captured with `subprocess.PIPE` and logged only on failure.
- **Resolved tree visible in that output.** The logged evidence carries the
  gate's resolved tree: root path (the push cwd), the `HEAD` sha at that root,
  the pushed sha, and executed-vs-cached for the full-suite entry — so "the gate
  ran and hit a cache for commit X" is distinguishable from "the gate never
  ran".
- **Executed-vs-cached is derived from the test cache, not wall-clock.** Using
  the read-only `skill/test_cache.py` API for the pushed git state: no valid
  entry before the push + a valid entry after ⇒ `executed`; a valid entry
  already present before the push ⇒ `cached`; still no entry after a successful
  push ⇒ `no-evidence` (warned, and never silently reported as green).
- **Read-only, never weakening.** The evidence path executes no test command
  itself, does not alter the cache, keeps `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` and friends as
  explicit escape hatches, and never turns a gate-accepted push into a failure.
- **Machine-readable.** The classification is added to
  `report["steps"]["push"]` so `implement.py finish --json` exposes it.
- **Tests, no timing proxies.** A test covers the three classifications
  (`executed` / `cached` / `no-evidence`) by staging cache entries in the
  fixture and asserting the logged line via `caplog` — no wall-clock assertions.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` (stderr
  logging), phase_finish Step 6 reporting (`report["steps"]["push"]`).
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `compute_git_state()`, `query_cached()` (read-only
  calls only; no changes expected).
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` and/or
  `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` — classification
  tests.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Capture `stderr` on success and `LOG.info` it (keep `LOG.error` on failure).
2. Before the push: compute the pushed git state's full-suite cache entry (if
   any) via `query_cached()`; after a successful push: re-query.
3. Emit one structured evidence line — e.g.
   `dev-push gate evidence: root=<cwd> head=<sha> pushed=<sha> full-suite=<executed|cached|no-evidence>`
   — and store the same dict under `report["steps"]["push"]["gate_evidence"]`.
4. Warn (not fail) on `no-evidence`, naming the commit, so a gate that did not
   run is visible without blocking recovery.

## Definition of Done

- Change-set tests green for all three classifications; a real finish over a
  cold cache logs `full-suite=executed`, over a warm cache `full-suite=cached`.

## Dependencies / Deliverables

- Prerequisite: the push-from-worktree item (the evidence must describe the
  pushed tree, which is the worktree).
- Deliverable: success-path hook logging + structured gate evidence in logs and
  `--json` output.

## Discovered from

`SA-0MVQHVCRE0070YO6` (F5, finish-gate abort contract), during its Step 9
post-push verification.

## Observation

`implement.py finish` pushed commit `a91334fe7` (branch
`wl-SA-0MVQHVCRE0070YO6-abort-invariants-for-the-finish-gate` →
`refs/heads/dev`) and reported success, but the **full suite cannot have run**
at that push:

- `phase_finish` timings: `main_checkout_guard.verifies` = `pre_push`
  14:06:45Z, `pre_worktree_removal` 14:07:12Z. The whole push window (commit →
  failed push → rebase → retry → ancestry check) is **~27 s**.
- A fresh full-suite run in this repository takes **706 s** (cached entry
  `0733bc36b99f`: `5241 passed, 14 skipped, 8 xfailed in 706.39s`).
- No new pytest full-scope entry was written to `.worklog/cache` during the
  push (the latest pytest `full` entry stays 13:45:34Z), and
  `test_cache.compute_git_state` keys on HEAD + dirty content, so a brand-new
  commit state cannot have been a cache hit.

## Contributing factor observed at the same time

The finish's verified local-`dev` fast-forward was **refused**
(`local_dev_fast_forward.reason = local_dev_diverged`; local `dev` =
`464f25a84`, `origin/dev` = `a624d18e`), so the main checkout stayed on the
**pre-push** commit. `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, …)` pushes with
`cwd=<main checkout>`, and `.githooks/pre-push` resolves both its runner
(`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) and its cache key from that cwd — i.e.
from the stale main checkout, not from the pushed tree. This is the same
gate-provenance class the epic fixes inside `phase_finish` (F7/F8), but on the
pre-push path.

## Why it matters

A dev push can be accepted with **no full-suite evidence for the pushed
tree**. A red tree then reaches `dev`, and the implement skill's Step 9
"cached green entry at the pushed commit" verification has nothing to consume.

## Suggested investigation

1. Reproduce with a push whose local-`dev` advance is refused (or a push from
   a worktree whose base is stale): instrument `.githooks/pre-push` to log
   `need_full_suite`, `repo_root`, the resolved runner and its exit code
   (currently `>/dev/null 2>&1` hides all of it).
2. Decide the authority: the hook must validate the **pushed tree** (derive
   the state from the pushed `<local_sha>`, not from the hook's cwd), or the
   push must be refused when the main checkout cannot be fast-forwarded.
3. Add a regression test: a push whose tree is red must be refused even when
   the main checkout's own state has a cached green full-suite entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A dev push whose pushed tree is red is refused by the pre-push hook, even when the main checkout sits on a different (cached-green) state.
- [ ] The hook's full-suite verdict is attributable to the pushed commit (the state it validated is recorded/logged).
- [ ] A green dev push leaves a cache entry for the pushed commit's state, so post-push verification and audits can consume it.
- [ ] Regression test covering the refused-fast-forward / stale-main-checkout case.
data.title: Dev-push full-suite gate did not execute for the pushed commit

## Discovered from

`SA-0MVQHVCRE0070YO6` (F5) during its Step 9 post-push full-suite verification.

## Observation

`python3 skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope full --json` at
`a91334fe7` (main checkout, `dev` == `origin/dev`) reported the pytest suite
**green** (`5265 passed, 14 skipped, 12 xfailed in 923.94s`) and every suite
command cached `exit 0` — yet the runner returned a **failed** verdict:

```
"live_repo_mutation": "live-repo mutation detected: the test suite changed a
guarded checkout for /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents. The run is failed so
a corrupted checkout cannot be pushed as green.
  moved ref      refs/heads/worklog/data: 8b9821e20747e0c764e71550b4f5b227caee73b0 -> 2a246a744917e4c2406a2475f6df42a6cfa55b3c"
```

`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` excludes `refs/worklog/` (`WORKLOG_REF_PREFIX`),
`refs/heads/dev` (`CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_EXACT`) and
`refs/remotes/origin/*` (`CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_NAMESPACES`) from the
mutation surface, but **not the Worklog data branch `refs/heads/worklog/data`**.
On a multi-agent host every `wl` write and every `wl sync` (any concurrent
session, including the pre-push hook's own sync) can move that ref inside a
run's guard window, which fails the run.

## Why it matters

- Full-suite evidence can never come out green on a busy host, so the
  dev-push / release gate and the audit skill's cached-run consumption see a
  red run for a green tree.
- It is the same class as the completed concurrency-exclusion work
  (`WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U`), just with a missing namespace: the worklog *data*
  branch is infrastructure state, not source, exactly like `refs/worklog/*`.

## Suggested change

Extend the concurrency exclusions in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` with
`refs/heads/worklog/data` (ideally as a namespace-style exclusion, e.g. a
`refs/heads/worklog/` prefix, so future worklog branches are covered), keeping
every other ref monitored. Add a regression test asserting that moving only
that ref is attributed to concurrency (excluded, reported as a note) while a
move of an ordinary source branch still fails the run — never a `wl-*`
name-pattern heuristic (AC4 of the ownership work).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A run in which only `refs/heads/worklog/data` moves reports green (excluded as concurrent infrastructure churn, surfaced as an informational note).
- [ ] A run in which an ordinary source branch ref moves is still failed as a mutation.
- [ ] `refs/worklog/*` behaviour is unchanged; no path/branch name-pattern heuristics introduced.
- [ ] Regression tests cover both directions (excluded vs. still-monitored).
data.title: live-repo guard flags concurrent refs/heads/worklog/data movement as a suite mutation

## Goal

Audit every existing caller of `StatusLifecycle` (and every path that sets a non-empty assignee) against the new release-by-default behaviour, migrating the ones that relied on the old default and explicitly opting out the intentional holds. Part of parent SA-0MVVEDK2Q008NDUH.

## Why

Flipping the default without auditing callers turns an invisible hold problem into an invisible release problem: a producer hold or a restore path could be wiped. The parent's acceptance criteria require every caller to be either updated or given an explicit, commented opt-out.

## Known caller surface (verify and complete by repo-wide grep)

| Caller | Current behaviour | Expected after this item |
|---|---|---|
| `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`phase_start`/`phase_finish`/`phase_abort`/`phase_parent`/drive finalise) | clears explicitly (`clear_assignee_on_exit=True` and per-call `assignee=""`) | drop the now-redundant flag; keep the explicit resets that serve the durable-write path |
| `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` (`start`/`finish`/`auto-complete`/`abort` + failure resets) | clears explicitly per call | drop redundant clearing where the helper now does it; comment anything kept |
| `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (claim + terminal verdicts) | clears on terminal; status-neutral claim via `--if-assignee ""` | unchanged behaviour, pinned by test |
| `skill/audit/scripts/verify_context_reduction.py` | restores a pre-existing assignee via raw `wl update` | explicit preserve/restore opt-out with an inline comment |
| `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` | creates recommendations with `--assignee Map` (intentional producer hold) | unchanged, pinned by a test |
| `skill/find-related`, `skill/refactor`, `skill/effort-and-risk`, `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` | use `StatusLifecycle` with no assignee | verify no assignee is set; no change expected |
| `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` | `--assignee ""` on close | unchanged |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A written inventory (in the parent item, `SA-0MVVEDK2Q008NDUH`) of every code path that sets a non-empty assignee, each classified as *must release on terminal* or *intentional hold* with a one-line justification, verified by repo-wide grep
- [ ] Every existing caller is audited; any caller relying on the old default is either updated or given an explicit opt-out with an inline comment explaining why
- [ ] Intentional holds are unaffected: producer-assignee holds (`Map`), `needsProducerReview` holds, `agent-log-review` creation assignees, and `verify_context_reduction`'s assignee restore all behave exactly as before (pinned by tests)
- [ ] `implement.py` drops the now-redundant `clear_assignee_on_exit=True`; `intake.py` and `audit_runner.py` per-call `assignee=""` are either removed as redundant or kept with a comment explaining the durable-write requirement
- [ ] The audit tier's status-neutral claim (`--if-assignee ""`, staying `completed`/`in_review`) keeps working unchanged
- [ ] No behaviour change is silent: every reviewed caller has a test that would fail if the assignee were left behind or wrongly cleared

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — largest caller, ~30 assignee resets across phase paths
- `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` — per-call clearing in `cmd_start`/`cmd_finish`/`cmd_auto_complete`/`cmd_abort`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — terminal verdict paths and the status-neutral claim
- `skill/audit/scripts/verify_context_reduction.py` — explicit preserve/restore opt-out
- `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` — intentional creation assignee
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_abort_clears_assignee.py`, `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_scripts_cwd.py`, `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` — per-skill pinning tests
- `tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py` — matrix rows added here as each caller is migrated

## Notes

- Depends on the default flip; do not migrate callers against the old default.
- "Intentional hold" means the item must stay on a scheduling hold: the producer's `Map` assignee, or `needsProducerReview=true`. A lingering agent assignee is never an intentional hold.
